Position Summary

We are seeking a dependable Process Operator to join our 3rd shift team in a food manufacturing environment. The Process Operator will be responsible for safely operating production equipment, accurately measuring and mixing spices and seasonings, monitoring the production process, and ensuring products meet quality and safety standards.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Operate and monitor processing and production equipment.
  • Measure, weigh, and blend spices, seasonings, and other ingredients according to established formulas.
  • Follow batch sheets, recipes, work instructions, and production schedules.
  • Load raw materials and ingredients into processing equipment.

  • Onsite, regular, and predictable attendance as scheduled is required.

job.title: Electro Plater
job.description:
Electroplating


M-T 6AM TO 4:30PM
Longwood

Position Overview
The Electroplating Laborer is responsible for safely supporting the electroplating process from start to finish. This position performs equipment safety checks, loads and unloads parts, assists with plating operations, inspects finished work, and prepares parts for shipment. The role also helps maintain a clean, organized, and safe shop environment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform daily safety inspections and checklists on all assigned equipment before beginning each shift.
  • Load and unload workpieces from electroplating equipment, including hooks, racks, bars, baskets, and barrels.
  • Move and immerse workpieces through the electroplating process, including cleaning, plating, pickling, and rinsing tanks, either manually or with a hoist while following established timed cycles.
  • Set and monitor tank temperatures according to required specifications.
  • Adjust DC rectifiers as needed to properly activate and maintain the electroplating process.
  • Remove plated parts from racks, hooks, bars, baskets, or barrels and inspect them for defects, including rough surfaces, thin plating, or other quality issues.
  • Dry plated parts using ovens, centrifugal dryers, or compressed air.
  • Perform quality inspections on finished parts and coordinate with Quality Control personnel for final inspection prior to packing.
  • Carefully wrap, package, and label finished parts in boxes or cartons for shipment.
  • Drain, clean, and refill plating tanks and solutions as directed.
  • Remove plating buildup from racks through approved chemical stripping procedures.
  • Immediately report damaged, worn, or malfunctioning equipment and any safety concerns to management.
  • Maintain a clean and organized work area, including removing trash and assisting with cleaning common areas, breakrooms, and bathrooms.
  • Follow all company safety procedures, PPE requirements, and chemical-handling guidelines.
  • Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned by management.

job.title: CNC Programmer - Aerospace
job.description:
The CNC Programmer develops part programs using Catia V5 to control the machining and processing of metal components on automated machine tools and equipment. This role uses Vericut software to validate programs before they are released to production.

Required Education and Experience

  • High school diploma or GED equivalent required.
  • Catia V5 6R2023 certification preferred.
  • Minimum of 3 years of aerospace CNC machine programming experience required.

Essential Functions

  • Analyze job orders, drawings, blueprints, and specifications to determine programming requirements.
  • Calculate dimensions, tool selections, machine speeds, and feed rates.
  • Create geometric layouts from graphic displays.
  • Determine reference points, machine cutting paths, and the sequence of machine operations.
  • Run computer simulations to confirm that programs and machinery function correctly and produce parts that meet customer specifications.
  • Observe trial runs with internal customers to verify program accuracy.
  • Revise programs to eliminate errors and retest to confirm that issues are resolved.
  • Modify existing programs to improve efficiency.
  • Collaborate with internal and external customers to support part programming and design requirements.
  • Perform other job-related duties as assigned.
Other Required Skills and Abilities
  • Ability to read and accurately interpret shop blueprints, sketches, and other technical instructions.
  • Demonstrated basic math skills, including addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and fraction conversions.
  • Experience troubleshooting production issues and editing programs.
  • Demonstrated reliability, with consistent performance and attendance.
  • Proficiency with Catia V5 required; experience with Vericut and iCAM preferred.

job.title: Vice President Datacenter Operations
job.description:
Nesco Data Center is seeking a VP of Data Center in the Greater Sterling VA area.

Vice President of Data Center Operations

Position Summary

The Vice President of Data Center Operations is a senior executive leadership position responsible for the strategic direction, operational excellence, financial performance, regulatory compliance, and overall management of multiple data center facilities throughout Virginia. This role provides executive oversight for data center operations in Ashburn, Herndon and Chantilly, Virginia, ensuring consistent execution of operational standards, customer satisfaction, infrastructure reliability, personnel development, and business growth initiatives.

The Vice President of Data Center Operations serves as the direct supervisor of all Facility Managers and is responsible for aligning operational objectives with corporate goals established by executive leadership. This position reports directly to the Executive Vice President and Ownership Group.

The successful candidate will possess extensive experience in mission-critical facilities, data center management, infrastructure operations, personnel leadership, budgeting, compliance, and vendor management.

Reporting Structure

Reports To:

  • Executive Vice President
  • Ownership Group

Direct Reports:

  • Facility Managers (Ashburn, VA)
  • Facility Managers (Hermitage, VA)
  • Facility Managers (Chantilly, VA)
  • Regional Operations Personnel
  • Facilities Engineering Leadership
  • Operations Support Staff (as assigned)

Primary Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership & Operations Management

  • Provide executive leadership and oversight for all operational activities across multiple data center facilities.
  • Develop and implement operational strategies that align with organizational growth objectives.
  • Establish and enforce company-wide operational standards, policies, procedures, and best practices.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on reliability, efficiency, scalability, and customer satisfaction.
  • Ensure consistency of operational execution across all facilities.
  • Lead long-term capacity planning, infrastructure planning, and facility growth initiatives.
  • Participate in executive planning meetings and strategic business development efforts.

Facility Oversight

  • Directly manage and mentor Facility Managers responsible for daily operations.
  • Conduct regular operational reviews and site assessments.
  • Monitor facility performance metrics, uptime statistics, service delivery standards, and operational KPIs.
  • Ensure all facilities maintain mission-critical operational readiness.
  • Oversee preventative maintenance programs and infrastructure lifecycle management.
  • Support commissioning, expansion, and modernization projects.

Financial Management & Budget Oversight

  • Develop, review, approve, and manage annual operating and capital budgets.
  • Analyze financial performance and operational expenditures across all facilities.
  • Identify opportunities for cost reduction and operational efficiency.
  • Review and approve major expenditures, procurement requests, and capital projects.
  • Collaborate with executive leadership on financial forecasting and strategic planning.
  • Ensure budget adherence and financial accountability throughout all locations.

Compliance, Risk Management & Governance

  • Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, local, and industry regulations.
  • Maintain adherence to operational standards, building codes, electrical codes, fire and life safety requirements, environmental regulations, and industry best practices.
  • Oversee compliance efforts related to:
    • SOC Audits
    • ISO Standards
    • Customer Compliance Requirements
    • OSHA Requirements
    • Environmental and Sustainability Programs
  • Lead risk assessment initiatives and business continuity planning.
  • Oversee disaster recovery, emergency response, and incident management programs.

Vendor & Contractor Management

  • Establish and maintain strategic relationships with key vendors, suppliers, contractors, and service providers.
  • Negotiate contracts, service agreements, and vendor partnerships.
  • Evaluate vendor performance and service-level compliance.
  • Approve contractor engagement and project execution plans.
  • Ensure third-party providers meet operational, security, and compliance requirements.

Infrastructure & Critical Systems Oversight

  • Maintain executive oversight of critical infrastructure systems including:
    • Electrical Distribution Systems
    • UPS Systems
    • Generators
    • Switchgear
    • Chillers
    • Cooling Infrastructure
    • Building Management Systems (Client)
    • Security Systems
    • Fire Detection and Suppression Systems
    • Structured Cabling Infrastructure
  • Ensure all critical systems operate within required service levels and uptime expectations.
  • Support infrastructure expansion and modernization initiatives.

Leadership & Talent Development

  • Build, mentor, and develop high-performing operations teams.
  • Establish leadership development programs for Facility Managers and technical personnel.
  • Conduct performance evaluations and succession planning activities.
  • Promote a culture of accountability, safety, professionalism, and operational excellence.
  • Support recruiting, onboarding, and retention initiatives.

Customer & Executive Engagement

  • Serve as the senior operational representative for key customers and stakeholders.
  • Participate in executive customer meetings and facility tours.
  • Address escalated operational issues and customer concerns.
  • Provide executive-level reporting to ownership and leadership teams.
  • Present operational performance metrics, risk assessments, and strategic recommendations.

Document Review & Executive Approvals

  • Review and approve operational documentation requiring executive authorization.
  • Evaluate facility-level requests, expenditures, policy changes, and project proposals.
  • Ensure operational decisions align with company standards and strategic objectives.
  • Provide final operational signoff for major projects, initiatives, and facility changes.

Safety & Security Leadership

  • Promote and enforce a culture of safety across all facilities.
  • Ensure compliance with workplace safety policies and procedures.
  • Oversee physical security standards and operational security practices.
  • Lead incident response efforts for major facility events or emergencies.
  • Support emergency preparedness and crisis management programs.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Engineering, Business Administration, Information Technology, Facilities Management, or related field.
  • 10+ years of progressive leadership experience within data center operations, mission-critical facilities, or related infrastructure environments.
  • 5+ years of senior management or executive leadership experience.
  • Proven experience managing multiple facilities and geographically distributed teams.
  • Strong financial management, budgeting, forecasting, and capital planning experience.
  • Extensive knowledge of mission-critical infrastructure systems.
  • Experience with regulatory compliance and operational audits.
  • Exceptional leadership, communication, and organizational skills.
  • Ability to travel regularly between Virginia facilities.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master's Degree in Business Administration (MBA), Engineering, or related field.
  • Uptime Institute Certifications.
  • Certified Data Centre Professional (CDCP).
  • Data Center Certified Associate/Professional Certifications.
  • Project Management Professional (PMP).
  • Certified Facility Manager (CFM).
  • Lean Six Sigma Certification.
  • Experience with hyperscale, colocation, enterprise, or wholesale data center environments.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Data Center Uptime Performance
  • Budget Performance and Cost Management
  • Operational Efficiency Metrics
  • Customer Satisfaction Scores
  • Audit and Compliance Results
  • Safety Incident Rates
  • Infrastructure Reliability Metrics
  • Employee Retention and Development Metrics
  • Preventative Maintenance Completion Rates
  • Capital Project Completion Performance

Core Competencies

  • Executive Leadership
  • Strategic Planning
  • Multi-Site Operations Management
  • Financial Acumen
  • Vendor Negotiation
  • Risk Management
  • Regulatory Compliance
  • Critical Infrastructure Management
  • Team Development
  • Customer Relationship Management
  • Process Improvement
  • Change Management
  • Business Continuity Planning
  • Decision-Making and Problem Solving

Work Environment

This position operates within mission-critical data center environments and corporate office settings. Regular travel between Ashburn, Hermitage, and Chantilly facilities is required. Occasional after-hours availability may be necessary to support operational incidents, executive initiatives, or emergency response situations.

The Vice President of Data Center Operations plays a critical leadership role in ensuring the organization's facilities operate safely, efficiently, profitably, and in accordance with the highest standards of reliability and operational excellence.

job.description:

The Maintenance Technician is responsible for completing maintenance assignments to build, repair and/or maintain all equipment in good operating condition as quickly and
accurately as possible, while keeping associated costs to a minimum to help
meet Plant goals. The Maintenance Technician is expected to be multi-skilled
and able to contribute to plant maintenance activities in a variety of craft
disciplines including Electrical, Mechanical, Maintenance and Industrial.

Essential Functions
  • Completes projects with minimal guidance showing a proactive attitude to minimizing equipment down time and lost production capability
  • Troubleshoots mechanical devices in operation. Dismantles and examines devices to gain access to and remove defective parts. Adjusts, repairs or replaces defective parts
  • Sets up and operates shop machinery such as lathe, drill press-grinders, band saws, cutting torch, welder, etc. Uses hand tools and pneumatic tools to modify or repair parts and equipment
  • Installs new or repairs/modifies hydraulic and pneumatic equipment as needed
  • Improves reliability and uptime of all equipment. Takes a proactive approach to equipment issues with a preventive maintenance mentality
  • Operates forklift and hydraulic working platform as needed
  • Researches supplies, parts and tools needed to complete work orders
  • Assists in identifying and maintaining an accurate inventory of parts
  • Contributes to upkeep and updating of required paperwork such as records, maintenance logs, documents, manuals, drawings, PM logs, etc.
  • Supports the vision, mission and guiding principles of the company
  • Follows applicable Safety, Health and Environmental rules and guidelines while performing job duties
  • Maintains departmental housekeeping
  • Other duties as assigned

QUALIFICATIONS:
Education and Experience
Technical School Degree or equivalent or relevant experience
- 5 years - Electrical, Mechanical, Maintenance and Industrial Operations
- 5 years - Process Improvements, Problem Solving Techniques, PLC Troubleshooting and Repairs
- Adherence to health and safety regulations (i.e. constant use of protective gear)
- Must be self-motivated and have organizational skills
- Time/Priority Management skills a must
- Must have Microsoft Office skills (word, excel, outlook)
- Knowledge of SAP preferred
- The employee must be able to read at a level of comprehension sufficient to meet job
requirements

Work Environment
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently exposed to:
  • Marked changes in temperature and humidity
  • Dust, fumes and/or airborne particles
  • Moving mechanical parts and vibration
  • The noise level in the work environment can be loud.
  • Be aware that in this position you will be working with powdered colorants and
  • more times than not, you will be grimy and dirty at the end of the day.

Physical Demands

  • While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; and talk or hear.

  • The employee is occasionally required to climb or balance.
  • The employee must frequently lift and/or move up to 55 pounds and frequently move more than 250 pounds with equipment.
  • Specific vision abilities required by this job include (20/40 vision) close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.
  • Requires the use of safety equipment as dictated by the work area such as safety glasses and shoes, dust mask, hardhat, respirator, face shield, hearing protection, chemical suit, gloves, aprons, etc.
  • Work is inside and the typical noise level is loud.
  • The employee is frequently exposed to wet and/or humid conditions, extreme heat, and risk of electrical shock.
  • The employee is occasionally exposed to high, precarious places; outside weather conditions; and explosives.
  • Regularly exposed to moving mechanical parts and fumes or airborne particles. The employee is frequently exposed to vibration.
  • The employee is occasionally exposed to toxic or caustic chemicals.

integrates EHS&S into all aspects of our operations. Each position at
responsible for complying with all applicable EHS&S requirements.

job.title: Fabricator / Fitter / Welder
job.description:
Fabricator / Welder

Clinton township, MI - Direct Hire

Position Type: Full-Time - Day shift

Compensation: $25.00 - $28.00 per hour

 

Basic Function

Responsible for all aspects of precision custom fabrication and advanced welding. This position requires a high-level blend of layout skill, blueprint proficiency, and multi-process welding expertise to fabricate jigs, fixtures, and production components to exact specifications.

Key Responsibilities & Accountabilities

  • Layout & Custom Fabrication: Read blueprints, engineering data, and drawings to take/read measurements and plan fabrication layouts and procedures. Layout, fit, and build precision jigs, fixtures, and tooling.

  • Multi-Process Welding: Determine appropriate welding equipment and methods based on project requirements. Perform high-quality MIG (GMAW), TIG (GTAW), and Resistance Spot Welding (RSW) in all positions (vertical, horizontal, overhead).

  • Specialized Materials: Execute precise TIG and MIG welding on stainless steel, aluminum, and mild steels, as well as specialized welding repairs/modifications on tool steel components.

  • Equipment & Machine Operation: Safely and efficiently operate standard metal fabrication machinery—including press brakes, shears, drill presses, and angle grinders —to prep, cut, shape, and finish materials.

  • Material Handling: Safely operate Hilos (forklifts) and other material handling equipment to move stock and tooling as needed.

  • Quality & Inspection: Align components using calipers, scales, and precision tools before clamping/welding. Test and inspect welded surfaces and structures to Client flaws, ensure parts are clean and burr-free, and maintain strict tolerances.

  • Problem Solving & Teamwork: Analyze and solve technical issues with fabrication projects. Actively participate in a team environment and communicate quality non-conformances effectively to supervisors and co-workers.

  • Shop Maintenance: Maintain all equipment and welding stations in a condition that does not compromise safety. Perform other duties as requested by management.

Skills & Qualifications

  • Experience: Proven experience as a Welder-Fabricator with a strong background in custom fixture/jig layout and building.

  • Equipment Proficiency: Strong hands-on experience using a variety of welding equipment, fabrication machinery (shears/brakes preferred), metal cutting tools, and manual hand tools.

  • Blueprint Reading & GD&T: Advanced ability to interpret complex industrial blueprints, welding symbols, technical schematics, GD&T (Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing) , Bills of Materials (BOM), and work instructions.

  • Measurement Mastery: Proficient with precision measuring tools including calipers, micrometers, tape measures, and squares.

  • Professional Attributes: Self-motivated, detail-oriented, analytical, and takes pride in producing high-quality work.

Education, Training & Certifications

  • Education: High School Diploma or GED required.

  • Certifications: AWS Certified for GMAW and GTAW in 1G through 4G positions highly preferred/required.

  • Experience: Verified prior welding and custom fabrication experience.

job.title: R&D Technical Associate
job.description:
Job Description:
The candidate will assume responsibility for the second-shift operation of a focused-ion beam scanning electron microscope (FIB-SEM) in support of the Qnity Leveraged Analytical Sciences group. This in-person position is located at the Experimental Station in Wilmington, DE. The candidate will work under the direction of experienced scientists to provide analytical support for Research and Development (R&D), Technical Service and Development (TS&D), and Manufacturing.

Key job responsibilities include:
• Prepare samples for analysis, following established procedures using equipment such as mechanical polishers, plasma or sputter coaters, and FIB-SEM cross-section milling and lift-out procedures.
• Perform FIB-SEM analyses including imaging, energy-dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDS), and electron backscattered diffraction (EBSD), and assess basic data quality.
• Review and organize collected data for reporting to customers.
• Perform routine instrument maintenance, following established procedures.
• Dispose of laboratory waste according to established protocols.
• Work second-shift hours and coordinate work with first-shift FIB-SEM operator.
• Adhere to all safety protocols.

Shift Details:
• Work hours/days: 40 hours/week
• M-F ~4:00 pm – 12:30 am (some flexibility may be available in daily start/finish times).
• Candidate will be trained during daytime hours (~8:30 am – 5 pm) for the first three months.
• In-person on-site position (no work from home).

Preferred Skills and Qualifications:
• Skills with electron microscopy.
• Experience with chemical handling in a laboratory setting.
• Demonstrate commitment to laboratory safety.
• Ability to work effectively in a team environment under tight timelines and competing priorities.
• Strong communication skills.

Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in chemistry, materials science, physics, engineering, or a related field or equivalent knowledge acquired through on-the-job training.

job.title: Quality Control Lead
job.description:
Title: Quality Control Lead
Location: Manufacturing Center
Department: Quality
Hours: Full Time
Shift Available:
Saturday, Sunday, Monday, and Tuesday 1:00 pm - 11:00 PM
The Opportunity:
Earth Breeze is seeking a Quality Control (QC) Lead to help ensure the quality, safety, and
consistency of our products, while also providing hands on leadership, training, and guidance to
our QC Technicians on the floor
This role is ideal for someone who is highly detail-oriented, analytical, and dependable.
Someone who takes pride in maintaining high standards and who will coach and mentor the
people around them. You'll thrive in this position if you're comfortable working independently,
guiding others, and speaking up when something needs attention. As a QC Lead reporting to
the QC Supervisor, you'll work side by side with the QC Techs in the quality lab and out on the
production floor to make sure procedures are being performed correctly and consistently, and
that the team is properly trained. You'll perform key quality checks yourself, which include
viscosity, pH, stir plate, and moisture testing, while also assessing how the rest of the team is
executing their duties, coaching them in real time and identifying trends that need to be
communicated to the QA Supervisor.
Responsibilities:
As a QC Lead at Earth Breeze, you will…
Team Leadership & Training
Work side by side with QC Technicians in the quality lab and out on the production floor,
observing and guiding their performance of daily and weekly duties.
Ensure QC Technicians are properly trained on department procedures and are
performing them correctly and consistently.
Assess technician performance, identify gaps in knowledge or technique, and provide
real-time coaching and correction.
Onboard and train new QC Technicians on procedures, equipment, and documentation
practices.
Serve as the go to resource for QC Technicians' questions during your shift.
Quality Testing & Monitoring
Perform and record quality control tests including viscosity, pH levels, stir plate/mixing
assessments, and moisture content.
Conduct retention checks and log results accurately.
Identify and communicate any out-of-spec results, trends, or anomalies promptly.
Trend Monitoring & Communication
Actively watch for trends across the QC department, quality lab, and production floor.
Such as recurring issues, technician performance patterns, or process shifts.
Communicate observed trends and floor level concerns clearly and promptly to the QA
Supervisor.
Escalate out of spec results or nonconformances immediately rather than holding them
for a later report.
Data Management
Accurately document and enter test results into logs, forms, and databases.
Track and identify production trends or shifts over time.
Collaboration & Communication
Partner with production team members to ensure parameters, specifications, and
procedures are consistently met.
Clearly communicate any quality concerns or deviations from standard process.
Participate in cross functional meetings or updates as required.
Workplace Monitoring & Safety
Regularly monitor the quality lab and production floor to ensure safety protocols are
followed.
Verify that team members are wearing proper PPE and report any safety concerns or
violations.
Reinforce company safety and hygiene policies as needed.
General Expectations
Maintain a high level of attention to detail and commitment to quality.
Be punctual, reliable, and accountable for all scheduled shifts.
Lead by example, working both independently and collaboratively to help the team
achieve production and quality goals.
Uphold and model company values around quality, communication, and safety.
About You:
You have…
Strong attention to detail, organizational skills, and an analytical mindset.
Demonstrated experience training, mentoring, or informally leading others.
A proactive approach to problem-solving and continuous improvement.
The ability to communicate clearly and professionally across teams, including up to
leadership.
A collaborative spirit and appreciation for safety and sustainability in manufacturing
environments.
The confidence to coach and redirect peers respectfully and constructively.

job.title: Digital Delivery Lead - Enterprise Website Migration (PMO)
job.description:
Digital Delivery Lead – Enterprise Website Migration

Overview

Client is undertaking a full rebuild of its global website, migrating to a composable Digital Experience Platform (DXP) that serves as the organization's primary digital presence. This role will own end-to-end delivery of the website launch, from initial planning through go-live execution.

This is a hands-on delivery leadership role focused on enterprise-scale website launches and platform migrations. The successful candidate will drive content readiness, stakeholder alignment, vendor coordination, governance, and launch planning across a complex global environment.

Core Responsibilities

Own end-to-end delivery of the new corporate website launch, including platform migration, content readiness, internal approvals, vendor coordination, and go-live execution.

Lead the content migration program, ensuring editorial content is audited, classified, produced, localized, and migrated with no gaps at launch.

Drive stakeholder alignment across Marketing, IT, Product, regional teams, and executive leadership, facilitating timely decisions and issue resolution.

Manage internal and external agencies, localization providers, and technical implementation partners throughout the project lifecycle.

Establish and maintain cross-functional governance processes, remove blockers, and proactively escalate risks.

Coordinate regional approval workflows, compliance requirements, localization activities, and stakeholder engagement across global markets.

Oversee go-live readiness activities, including QA, rollback planning, SEO validation, URL mapping, and launch-day execution.

Essential Qualifications, Skills, and Technologies

10+ years of experience in digital project delivery, web platform launches, or digital transformation programs.

Proven track record delivering enterprise website migrations on time and within budget.

Experience leading at least two full corporate website launches or platform migrations for enterprise-scale organizations involving 500+ pages and multiple markets.

Deep understanding of content operations, including CMS platforms, PIM systems, DAM platforms, localization workflows, and editorial governance.

Experience with DXP and composable architecture environments, with a strong understanding of modern content platforms.

Experience managing content migration programs, including audit, classification, content production, and localization processes.

Strong stakeholder management experience with C-level leaders, including presentations to CMOs, CIOs, and steering committees.

Experience coordinating multiple internal stakeholders and external vendors simultaneously in complex enterprise environments.

Experience working within global organizations that require regional approvals, compliance management, and localization coordination.

Knowledge of SEO migration strategies, URL mapping, 301 redirects, and launch practices designed to minimize performance regression.

Experience delivering projects with fixed launch deadlines and running governance structures that drive decisions and accountability.

Ability to be physically present in Westerville, Ohio, with onsite participation during critical phases of the project.

Availability to start within the next 2–3 weeks.

Preferred Skills or Experience

Background in a digital or web agency environment with experience delivering enterprise website launches.

Experience leading large-scale digital transformation initiatives within a management consulting environment.

Prior experience as a Head of Digital, Director of Web, or similar digital leadership role.

Work Details

Location: Westerville, Ohio.

Onsite role requiring a minimum of 3 days per week in the office, with up to 5 days per week during critical project phases.

Start date: Available within the next 2–3 weeks.

job.title: File Clerk
job.description:
File & Records Support Specialist

Position Overview

We are seeking a detail-oriented and organized professional to support physical and digital records management, file organization, document retention, and data tracking. This position will primarily involve locating, organizing, documenting, boxing, and preparing account files for retention or destruction.

The ideal candidate is comfortable performing repetitive, detail-focused work, has experience with filing systems, and can accurately maintain tracking information in Microsoft Excel.

Work Schedule & Location

  • Work Model: 100% On-site
  • Schedule: Monday – Friday, 5 days per week
  • Location: 66 South Pearl Street, Albany, NY

Key Responsibilities

File & Records Management

  • Search for and retrieve physical files from shelving based on closed-account filing lists.
  • Review and organize closed account files according to established retention requirements.
  • Identify and shred files that have exceeded the required account retention period.
  • Package closed files that are not eligible for destruction into boxes organized by year closed.
  • Label boxes accurately with:
    • Account numbers
    • Account closure dates
    • Scheduled destruction dates
  • Remove and relocate files from designated shelving areas to accommodate facilities maintenance.
  • Condense and reorganize remaining open-account files in numerical account order.
  • Prepare file boxes for shipment to off-site retention facilities as needed.
  • Follow established off-site storage instructions and packaging requirements.

Data Entry & Tracking

  • Log files and box labels accurately using Microsoft Excel spreadsheets.
  • Maintain organized and accurate records of files being retained, relocated, or destroyed.
  • Ensure physical records correspond with information documented in tracking spreadsheets.

Qualifications

  • Previous experience with physical and/or digital filing systems preferred.
  • Comfortable working with Microsoft Excel spreadsheets.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to accurately organize files by account number, year, and retention requirements.
  • Ability to remain focused and productive while performing repetitive tasks.
  • Comfortable working independently on structured, detail-oriented assignments.
  • Ability to follow document retention and file management procedures.
  • Ability to lift and move boxes weighing approximately 10–15 pounds.

Required Prescreen Questions

The following questions must be answered and submitted with the candidate's resume:

  1. What experience do you have with physical and digital filing systems?
  2. Are you comfortable using Excel spreadsheets?
  3. Can you lift boxes weighing 10–15 pounds?
  4. How do you keep yourself focused and motivated when performing repetitive tasks?
  5. Are you organized? This position will require you to pull files from shelving, organize them into boxes by year closed, and log the files and corresponding box labels in a spreadsheet.

job.title: Critical Facilities Engineer (Datacenter)
job.description:
Nesco Data Center and Infrastructure is seeking a Mission Critical Data Center Engineer in the Greater Ashburn VA area.
 

Mission Critical Data Center Engineer – Night Shift
 

We are seeking an experienced Mission Critical Data Center Engineer to support the safe, reliable, and continuous operation of a mission-critical data center environment on the night shift. This position is responsible for monitoring, operating, troubleshooting, and maintaining critical facility infrastructure and mechanical/electrical systems that support 24x7 data center operations.

The ideal candidate has hands-on experience working in a mission-critical environment and understands the importance of preventative maintenance, operational procedures, emergency response, documentation, and strict adherence to safety and change-control processes.

The successful candidate will have a strong facilities background and experience with the infrastructure systems that provide power, cooling, environmental control, fire/life safety, and building management for a high-availability data center.

Pay range is $42-56/hr + 10% ND

 

Mission Critical Facilities Operations

  • Monitor and operate critical data center infrastructure and building systems during the overnight shift.

  • Perform routine inspections of electrical, mechanical, HVAC, and life-safety systems.

  • Monitor facility conditions, alarms, temperatures, humidity, power utilization, and equipment status.

  • Respond promptly to alarms, abnormal operating conditions, equipment failures, and facility emergencies.

  • Perform equipment rounds and document operating conditions, readings, deficiencies, and corrective actions.

  • Maintain situational awareness of facility load, capacity, redundancy, and equipment operating status.

  • Follow established operating procedures, emergency operating procedures, and standard operating procedures.

  • Participate in 24x7 on-call and/or emergency response activities as required.

Electrical Systems

Experience operating and/or maintaining critical electrical infrastructure such as:

  • Utility service and electrical distribution systems

  • Switchgear and switchboards

  • Automatic Transfer Switches (ATS)

  • UPS systems and battery systems

  • Power Distribution Units (PDUs)

  • Remote Power Panels (RPPs)

  • Transformers

  • Generators and emergency power systems

  • Automatic transfer and emergency power systems

  • Electrical panels and distribution equipment

  • 3-phase electrical systems

  • Power monitoring and metering systems

The engineer should understand electrical distribution, redundancy concepts, load balancing, power flow, and the risks associated with working around energized equipment.


Mechanical / Cooling Systems

Experience with mission-critical cooling infrastructure, including:

  • Chillers and chilled-water systems

  • Cooling towers and condenser-water systems

  • CRAH/CRAC units

  • Pumps and pumping systems

  • Computer Room Air Handling systems

  • Air-handling and ventilation systems

  • Humidification/dehumidification systems

  • Heat exchangers

  • Cooling Distribution Units (CDUs)

  • Direct-to-chip and/or liquid cooling systems is a plus

  • Building HVAC systems

  • Temperature and humidity control systems

Building Management & Monitoring Systems

  • Monitor and respond to alarms through Client/EPMS/DCIM platforms.

  • Review trends and operating data to identify abnormal conditions before they become failures.

  • Understand critical alarm priorities and escalation procedures.

  • Document alarm events, equipment status, and corrective actions.

  • Work with remote monitoring and control systems to verify equipment operation.

  • Experience with systems such as Client, EPMS, DCIM, or similar monitoring platforms is strongly preferred.

Preventative & Corrective Maintenance

  • Perform or coordinate preventative maintenance on critical infrastructure.

  • Assist vendors and contractors during scheduled maintenance activities.

  • Troubleshoot equipment and determine appropriate corrective actions.

  • Verify completed maintenance activities and return equipment to normal operating configuration.

  • Maintain accurate maintenance records and equipment documentation.

  • Identify recurring equipment issues and recommend improvements.

  • Support reliability and continuous-improvement initiatives.

Emergency Response

  • Respond immediately to critical alarms and facility emergencies.

  • Execute emergency operating procedures and established escalation protocols.

  • Troubleshoot power, cooling, environmental, and mechanical failures.

  • Communicate effectively with management, security, vendors, customers, and other technical personnel during incidents.

  • Participate in incident investigations and root-cause analysis.

  • Maintain composure and sound judgment during high-pressure situations.

Change Management & Documentation

  • Follow formal change-management procedures for all critical facility work.

  • Review Method of Procedures (MOPs), Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), and Emergency Operating Procedures (EOPs).

  • Participate in MOP/EOP reviews and execution.

  • Maintain shift logs, equipment logs, work orders, incident reports, and operational documentation.

  • Provide detailed shift turnover to incoming engineering personnel.

  • Ensure all work is performed in accordance with site procedures and established safety requirements.

Required Qualifications

  • 3–7+ years of experience in data center facilities, mission-critical facilities, critical infrastructure, industrial facilities, semiconductor facilities, hospitals, power plants, or a similarly complex operating environment.

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.

  • Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Facilities Management, Engineering Technology, HVAC, or a related technical discipline preferred.

  • Equivalent military, technical-school, apprenticeship, or hands-on mission-critical experience may be considered in lieu of a formal degree.

  • Demonstrated experience operating and troubleshooting critical electrical and/or mechanical systems.

  • Ability to read and understand electrical one-line diagrams, mechanical drawings, equipment manuals, and technical documentation.

  • Strong understanding of electrical and mechanical safety practices.

  • Experience working in a 24x7 mission-critical environment preferred.

  • Ability to work independently during an overnight shift while maintaining strong communication with day-shift personnel and management.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

  • Strong attention to detail and documentation skills.

  • Ability to prioritize multiple alarms, work orders, and operational issues based on criticality.

Preferred Qualifications & Certifications

Preferred candidates may possess one or more of the following:

  • Data Center Certified Associate (DCCA) or equivalent data center certification

  • Certified Data Center Professional (CDCP)

  • Certified Data Centre Specialist (CDCS)

  • BICSI credentials

  • OSHA 10 or OSHA 30

  • EPA 608 certification

  • Electrical or HVAC certifications

  • NFPA training

  • Generator or UPS manufacturer training

  • Client/Client/EPMS/DCIM training

  • Electrical safety / NFPA 70E training

  • Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) training

  • CPR/AED/First Aid certification

  • Facilities or stationary engineering certification

  • Journeyman electrical, HVAC, or mechanical license is a plus

Safety & Compliance

  • Strictly follow OSHA, NFPA, site-specific safety requirements, and company policies.

  • Follow Lockout/Tagout and electrical safe-work practices.

  • Utilize appropriate PPE when performing inspections, maintenance, and troubleshooting.

  • Maintain a safety-first mindset when working around energized electrical equipment, rotating machinery, high-voltage systems, pressurized systems, refrigerants, and other hazards.

  • Report unsafe conditions immediately.

  • Participate in safety meetings, training, audits, and emergency drills.

Night Shift Requirements

  • Night shift availability is required.

  • Ability to remain alert, attentive, and responsive throughout an overnight shift.

  • Comfortable working independently with limited onsite management supervision.

  • Ability to respond to critical alarms and emergencies at any time during the shift.

  • Willingness to work weekends, holidays, overtime, and emergency call-ins when required by site operations.

  • Reliable attendance and punctuality are critical to maintaining continuous data center coverage.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is a hands-on mission-critical facilities professional, not simply a general building engineer. They understand that uptime, redundancy, safety, documentation, and procedural discipline are paramount in a data center environment.

The strongest candidates will have experience operating a data center or similarly critical facility, understand UPS, generators, switchgear, PDUs, chillers, CRAH/CRAC systems, Client/EPMS/DCIM, emergency procedures, preventative maintenance, and electrical/mechanical systems, and can independently manage the facility during an overnight shift.

job.title: R&D Technical Associate - Wafer Fab
job.description:
Job Description:
The candidate will assume responsibility for the second-shift operation of a Time-of-Flight Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry (ToF-SIMS) instrument in support of the Qnity Leveraged Analytical Sciences group. This in-person position is located at the Experimental Station in Wilmington, DE. The candidate will work under the direction of experienced scientists to provide analytical support for Research and Development (R&D), Technical Service and Development (TS&D), and Manufacturing.

Key job responsibilities include:
• Prepare samples for ToF-SIMS analysis following established procedures, including sample mounting, handling of semiconductor wafers, powders, films, coatings, and other materials, and preparation of air- or contamination-sensitive samples when needed.
• Perform routine ToF-SIMS analyses, including surface spectroscopy, chemical imaging, and depth profiling using established analytical methods.
• Operate the ToF-SIMS instrument during second-shift hours, including sample loading, vacuum system operation, beam tuning, data acquisition, and basic instrument checks.
• Support routine instrument maintenance and housekeeping activities following established procedures. Coordinate service or troubleshooting needs with first-shift operators and scientists.
• Document experimental conditions, sample information, observations, and analysis results in appropriate laboratory systems.
• Prepare analysis summaries and contribute to technical reports, including discussion of results, observations, and potential analytical findings.
• Dispose of laboratory waste according to established protocols.
• Work second-shift hours and coordinate work with first-shift scientists to ensure continuity of lab operations.

Shift Details:
• Work hours/days: 40 hours/week
• M-F ~4:00 pm – 12:30 am (some flexibility may be available in daily start/finish times)
• Candidate will be trained during daytime hours (~8:30 am – 5 pm) for the first three months.

Preferred Skills and Qualifications:
• Strong skills in sample preparation, careful sample handling, and safe chemical handling.
• Experience preparing and handling whole wafers, diced wafer pieces, thin films, and other materials commonly encountered in semiconductors or advanced materials applications.
• Experience with analytical instrumentation in a chemical, materials, or surface analysis laboratory setting.
• Familiarity with high-vacuum instrumentation, mass spectrometry, surface analysis, spectroscopy, microscopy, or related techniques is preferred.
• Ability to document analytical results and prepare clear, concise technical reports.
• Demonstrated commitment to laboratory safety and responsible adherence to all safety protocols.
Good attention to detail and ability to follow established procedures consistently.
• Ability to work effectively in a team environment under tight timelines and competing priorities.
• Strong communication skills and willingness to coordinate closely with scientists and project stakeholders.

Minimum Qualifications:
• Bachelor of Science (B.S.) in chemistry, materials science, physics, engineering, or a related field, or equivalent knowledge acquired through on-the-job training.

job.title: Hose Former
job.description:
ENERAL SUMMARY
Responsible for the efficient manufacture and quality forming of production parts within the assigned department.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES (Duties required for successful job performance):
  1. Check specifications as to job and perform numbers.
  2. Retrieve proper pre-form and guide onto mandrel using lubricant as necessary.
  3. Position loaded mandrels in curing rack for curing. Move curing rack into autoclave when full.
  4. Remove curing rack from autoclave to proper work area.
  5. Position mandrel bars for unloading. Remove formed hose from mandrel, place into proper container.
  6. Position full baskets with proper job and employee clock numbers.
  7. Identify parts baskets with proper job and employee clock numbers.
  8. Set up curing racks per production and supervisor guidance.
  9. Replenish lubricant in trough as needed.
  10. Perform all operations according to standard practice or as directed by supervisor to produce quality parts.
  11. Fill out required paperwork as necessary.
  12. Record cure charts as required.
  13. Perform other miscellaneous duties required but not listed above.





REQUIRED EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE (These are the traditional minimum, or required, bona-fide occupational qualifications and other requirements of most people in this job).
  1. High School Diploma or GED required. Previous manufacturing experience preferred (particularly in a team environment).
  2. NCRC certified preferred.
REQUIRED SKILLS AND ABILITIES (Those needed to perform the essential functions of the job).
  1. Interpersonal Skills Must be able to read and write at a medium level for the purpose of understanding and applying quality documentation and standard operating procedures, along with completion of job / time reporting.
  2. Problem-solving May be asked to participate in continuous improvement activities and perform basic mathematics.
  3. Physical / Mental / Visual abilities Duties of job require periods of standing, use of hands (pushing and pulling > 50 lbs.) and fingers, bending and reaching, lifting (> 50lbs.) and movement of materials frequently. Must be able to visually interpret work instructions.
REQUIRED DECISION-MAKING AND ORGANIZATION IMPACT (Describe the typical types of decisions made by employees in this job and the likely impact of those decisions on the Company).
  1. The position will decide on a daily basis the acceptable level of quality for finished product to be shipped to the customer.
  2. This determination will be based upon interpretation of the customer specifications and past experience.
  3. Customer rejections of finished product could incur additional costs and may jeopardize the sourcing of business to the company.
REPORTING RELATIONSHIPS (Indicate job titles for this job's supervisor and direct reports).
  1. Directly Reports To: Group Leader / Shift Supervisor
  2. Indirectly Reports To: Business Unit Manager- II
WORKING CONDITIONS (Describe the environment within which the work is performed).
  1. Work time will be spent in general factory floor environments.
  2. Temperature and noise may vary depending on external environmental conditions.
  3. Lack of attention and carelessness may result in personal injury to self or others.

Position Overview

The successful candidate will spearhead the organization's accounting operations, ensuring accuracy in financial reporting, month-end close processes, and team management. This role demands oversight of accounts payable (AP), accounts receivable (AR), general ledger, inventory accounting, and financial reporting. Close collaboration with the CFO is essential for budgeting, forecasting, tax compliance, financial analysis, and driving business growth initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead daily accounting operations, including AP, AR, general ledger management, and reconciliations.

job.title: Strategic Technology Program Manager
job.description:
The Opportunity

We're looking for an experienced technology program leader who can help turn strategic ideas into real business outcomes.

This isn't a traditional project manager role focused primarily on schedules, sprint ceremonies, or status reports. You'll work directly with technology leadership and business stakeholders to drive important initiatives across the organization, from planning and prioritization through implementation, adoption, and measurable results.

The right person will enjoy bringing order to ambiguity, solving problems, working across departments, and creating practical processes where they don't already exist.

Think of this as a combination of strategic program management, technology transformation, and internal Chief of Staff support.

What You'll Do

Program & Delivery Leadership

  • Own planning and execution for technology initiatives that involve multiple business and technical teams.
  • Establish clear objectives, priorities, dependencies, risks, responsibilities, and desired business outcomes.
  • Coordinate work across application development, data, infrastructure, outside vendors, and business stakeholders.
  • Maintain visibility into key milestones, decisions, risks, and blockers while driving issues toward resolution.
  • Provide leadership with concise updates focused on progress, business impact, risks, and next steps.
  • Introduce the appropriate level of project discipline without creating unnecessary process or bureaucracy.

Business Implementation & Change

  • Make sure new solutions are successfully adopted by the organization rather than simply delivered by the technology team.
  • Coordinate rollout readiness, training, communications, process changes, adoption activities, and handoff into ongoing operations.
  • Work with department leaders to understand how workflows will change and what employees need in order to successfully adopt new capabilities.
  • Help define current-state measures and expected outcomes so the organization can evaluate the business impact of new initiatives.

Process Improvement & Playbook Development

  • Build practical templates, processes, and repeatable playbooks that make future technology implementations easier and more consistent.
  • Identify tools and processes that improve planning, tracking, communication, prioritization, and delivery.
  • Continuously refine the organization's approach based on lessons learned from completed initiatives.
  • Bring additional structure to areas that are currently informal while maintaining speed and flexibility.

Technology Strategy & Portfolio Support

  • Partner closely with technology leadership to translate strategic priorities into actionable initiatives.
  • Maintain visibility into upcoming work, active initiatives, backlog, available capacity, and competing priorities.
  • Help evaluate and sequence initiatives based on business value, dependencies, resources, and organizational priorities.
  • Work across business functions to understand upcoming needs and align them with the broader technology roadmap.

Vendor & Partner Coordination

  • Coordinate outside technology vendors and implementation partners involved in active initiatives.
  • Maintain visibility into vendor commitments, milestones, dependencies, and deliverables.
  • Work with internal leadership and procurement partners to resolve issues and maintain accountability.
  • Help ensure outside resources remain aligned with internal capacity and business objectives.

Risk & Governance

  • Maintain appropriate project documentation, approvals, decision records, and delivery controls.
  • Assist with internal and external audit requests related to technology initiatives.
  • Develop lightweight governance practices that reduce operational risk without unnecessarily slowing execution.

What We're Looking For

  • 5–8+ years of experience leading technology projects, programs, transformation initiatives, or other complex cross-functional work.
  • Experience owning initiatives that involve both technology teams and business stakeholders.
  • Demonstrated ability to work directly with senior leaders and executives.
  • Strong experience influencing people and driving results without relying on direct authority.
  • Ability to operate successfully in environments where project processes and standards are still evolving.
  • Strong organizational skills with excellent follow-through.
  • Comfortable entering ambiguous situations, identifying what's missing, and creating practical solutions.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to simplify complex topics for leadership.
  • Ability to build credibility and productive relationships across departments.
  • Bachelor's degree in information systems, business, a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.

Nice to Have

  • Experience implementing AI, automation, or technology-enabled process improvement initiatives.
  • Change management or large-scale business adoption experience.
  • Experience supporting M&A due diligence or post-acquisition integrations.
  • Background in insurance, financial services, fintech, or another regulated industry.
  • Experience developing repeatable implementation or delivery playbooks.
  • Data governance exposure.

job.title: Operations Manager
job.description:
Nesco Resource is seeking an Operations Manager to join our client's team located in New Haven County.
    
SUMMARY
We are seeking a hands-on Operations Manager to lead daily manufacturing and supply chain operations for a well-established, highly technical manufacturer serving industries including Aerospace, Defense, Medical, and other advanced technology markets. The ideal candidate is a hands-on, results-driven manufacturing leader who is comfortable managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced technical environment. This individual will bring strong problem-solving abilities, operational discipline, and a commitment to quality, customer satisfaction, continuous improvement, and employee development.

RESPONSIBILITIES
•    Lead day-to-day manufacturing operations across Production, Quality, Materials/Purchasing, Shipping, Tooling, Maintenance, and Facilities
•    Establish operational priorities, KPIs, and accountability systems
•    Drive improvements in throughput, labor efficiency, scrap reduction, setup time, and schedule attainment
•    Implement and strengthen Lean Manufacturing, Kaizen, and continuous improvement initiatives
•    Improve workflow, manufacturing processes, inventory management, and facility utilization
•    Drive initiatives toward 99% on-time delivery
•    Support compliance with ISO and/or AS9100 quality standards
•    Partner with Quality leadership to improve KPIs, corrective actions, response times, and PPM performance
•    Oversee production planning, purchasing, inventory management, and supplier performance
•    Support cost-reduction and supply-chain optimization initiatives
•    Coach and develop managers, supervisors, and production personnel
•    Partner with Human Resources on hiring, workforce planning, employee development, and performance management
•    Promote a safe, professional, accountable, and collaborative manufacturing environment

QUALIFICATIONS
•    Bachelor's degree required; Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, or related discipline preferred
•    10+ years of manufacturing leadership experience within a technical manufacturing environment
•    Minimum 5 years of management experience leading cross-functional operations teams
•    Strong background in Lean Manufacturing, Kaizen, and continuous improvement
•    Experience with ERP/MRP systems, production scheduling, inventory management, and manufacturing KPIs
•    Working knowledge of ISO and/or AS9100 quality systems preferred
•    Strong analytical, organizational, communication, and leadership abilities
•    Ability to drive accountability and build high-performing teams
•    Advanced Microsoft Excel and business reporting skills preferred

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
•    Direct hire with competitive compensation and benefits package including medical, dental, vision, disability and life insurance, 401(k) with company match, paid holidays and vacation, tuition reimbursement and career growth opportunities.
•    1st shift, Monday – Friday, 8am – 5pm
•    Salary range: $150K; may be willing to go higher for the right candidate
•    Must pass drug and background screening

Position Summary:
Assembles and fastens coil springs in wood frame.

Position Responsibilities:
  • Gather all supplies including springs, staples, nails, no-sags, FLW, no-sag clips and vertex clips and have them ready at work station as needed.
  • Get frames from webbing back to work station as they come through process.
  • Consult standards/notes for each piece to ensure quality and accurateness.
  • Apply nails, strings, and springs in each piece in accordance to Vanguard Quality standards.

  • Push frame to loading area for inter-company truck.
  • Scan the piece completed in the system once finished with the piece.
  • Perform all duties safely and report any safety hazards to your immediate supervisor.
  • Complete other assigned duties as directed by supervisor.
  • Place springs in frame and tie down using eight-way hand tie method.
  • Put cardboard on frames where needed.
  • Maintains neat and orderly work station.
  • Wear required safety glasses and work shoes; works safely and reports unsafe conditions to Dept. Supervisor.
  • Performs other duties as required by supervisor.
Essential Skills and Experience:
  • English required for reading tickets and instructions.
  • Must be knowledgeable in eight-way hand tie method.
Valued but not Required Skills and Experience:
  • Previous knowledge of eight-way hand tie method.
Physical demands and work environment:
  • Lift / Carry: Frequently lifting 35 – 50 lbs. onto and off work station; occasionally lifting in excess of 50 lbs.; team lift greater weights.

job.description:
IT Project Manager III

Overview

Client is seeking an IT Project Manager III to lead cross-functional projects of medium to high complexity from initiation through completion. This role partners with stakeholders, technical teams, cybersecurity leadership, vendors, and business units to deliver technology projects that align with project objectives, governance standards, and budget expectations.

The successful candidate will manage software, hardware, ERP, security, and other IT-focused initiatives while driving communication, risk management, financial oversight, project planning, and stakeholder alignment. This position requires strong project management discipline, excellent communication skills, and the ability to operate effectively within a matrix organization.

Core Responsibilities

• Manage assigned IT PMO projects with minimal supervision, ensuring alignment to project scope, objectives, schedules, budgets, and desired outcomes.

• Lead cross-functional project teams and coordinate activities across stakeholders, business partners, technical resources, and vendors.

• Develop and maintain detailed project plans and schedules to track progress and ensure successful project delivery.

• Organize and facilitate status meetings, project reviews, workshops, training sessions, and governance activities.

• Prepare and deliver weekly project status reporting and presentations covering timelines, accomplishments, health indicators, upcoming milestones, risks, and issues.

• Monitor project scope, schedule, costs, risks, actions, decisions, and opportunities, implementing appropriate controls and mitigation strategies.

• Manage project-related financial processes, including forecasting, budget tracking, accruals, reclassifications, and variance reporting.

• Coordinate with third-party vendors and system integrators to ensure alignment with project deliverables, statements of work, invoicing requirements, and timelines.

• Build consensus among stakeholders, facilitate issue resolution, support escalation processes, and ensure effective communication across project teams.

• Create, maintain, and store project documentation and project records in accordance with established governance standards.

• Promote and enforce project management best practices while supporting successful project execution and closure.

Essential Qualifications, Skills, and Technologies

• Bachelor's degree required.

• Project Management Professional (PMP) certification required.

• 5 to 7 years of experience managing multiple software, hardware, ERP, and/or technology projects.

• Proven experience managing multi-disciplinary teams across functional work streams.

• Proven experience managing implementation projects involving multiple system integrators with shared responsibilities.

• Proven experience leading software releases, ERP implementations, and/or security-focused projects.

• Experience applying project management best practices to guide projects through planning, execution, monitoring, and delivery.

• Strong understanding of project scope, cost, and schedule management, including control of project triple constraints.

• Experience performing risk management, issue management, change control, and stakeholder management activities.

• Understanding of the Software Development Lifecycle (SDLC).

• Intermediate to advanced proficiency with Microsoft Project.

• Ability to identify, document, communicate, and manage project risks, issues, and problems.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present project information clearly and concisely.

• Strong organizational, time management, and documentation skills.

• Self-motivated, detail-oriented, collaborative, and able to perform effectively in dynamic and complex environments.

Preferred Skills or Experience

• Experience within the energy industry.

• Experience working in an Information Technology environment.

• Experience working with or managing projects supporting Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, and/or Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) teams.

• Master's degree.

Work Details

• No direct supervisory responsibilities or direct reports.

job.title: Quality Technican
job.description:
We are seeking a Quality/Supplier Quality professional to support manufacturing operations by monitoring incoming supplier products and in-process materials to ensure parts are available for production and meet established quality requirements. This position will identify and resolve issues involving nonconforming parts, documentation discrepancies, shipping problems, and supplier-related quality concerns.

The ideal candidate will have 2–3 years of experience in quality inspection, supplier quality, quality assurance, or aerospace/manufacturing, with the ability to read complex engineering drawings and use inspection equipment.

Key Responsibilities

  • Monitor incoming supplier products and in-process materials for quality, documentation, and availability issues.
  • Identify, investigate, and resolve day-to-day product discrepancies and nonconformances.
  • Review parts and associated paperwork to determine whether materials can be released for manufacturing.
  • Communicate directly with suppliers to resolve quality, documentation, delivery, and product issues.
  • Support nonconforming material processes and assist with product containment activities.
  • Help validate supplier and internal corrective actions and follow up on resolution effectiveness.
  • Coordinate with Quality, Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and other internal teams to resolve production-impacting issues.
  • Review First Article Inspection (FAI/FAIR), PPAP, and other supplier quality documentation.
  • Assist with customer-returned material and coordinate related internal and external activities.
  • Read and interpret engineering drawings, blueprints, route sheets, specifications, and manufacturing documentation.
  • Perform or support visual and dimensional inspections using appropriate inspection tools.
  • Apply GD&T principles and applicable quality standards when evaluating parts.
  • Participate in root-cause/problem-solving activities, Kaizen events, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Maintain 5S standards and contribute to a safe, organized, and efficient work environment.
  • Provide support, training, and knowledge sharing to other team members as needed.

Required Qualifications

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required; additional technical education preferred.
  • 2–3 years of related experience in:
    • Quality Inspection
    • Supplier Quality
    • Quality Assurance
    • Manufacturing Quality
    • Aerospace Manufacturing
  • Experience working in a manufacturing, aerospace, engineering, or quality environment.
  • Experience using inspection tools and methods to evaluate manufactured parts.
  • Ability to read and understand complex blueprints, engineering drawings, specifications, route sheets, and work instructions.
  • Working knowledge of shop mathematics, including basic trigonometry.
  • Strong problem-solving and communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with suppliers and cross-functional internal teams.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office tools.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Aerospace manufacturing experience.
  • Supplier Quality experience.
  • Experience with FAI/FAIR, PPAP, Client/nonconformance, corrective actions, and containment.
  • Knowledge of GD&T / ASME Y14.5.
  • Experience with calipers, micrometers, gauges, CMMs, or other inspection equipment.
  • Knowledge of military/aerospace specifications and standards.
  • Experience with continuous improvement, Kaizen, or 5S.

Compensation

  • Pay Rate: $28–$32/hour
  • $30–$32/hour: Candidates should have directly related inspection or supplier experience, particularly Supplier Quality, Quality Assurance, aerospace, or manufacturing experience.
  • RPO Hire

Important Eligibility Requirement

This position is subject to meeting applicable U.S. Export Compliance and/or U.S. Government Contracting citizenship eligibility requirements.

job.title: Quality Inspector
job.description:
Monday-Friday - 6AM-2:30PM, OT as needed.

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions.

Job Summary:
The Quality Inspector will check the quality of all products as well as production procedures. The role will be an advocate for quality in our business. The Quality Inspector will ensure that products are made of flawless materials in compliance with customer specifications.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
Inspect, test and measure materials or products and accurately record inspection and test data. This includes measuring products using rulers, calipers, gauges, coordinate measuring machines (CMM), thread gauges, gauge pins, optical comparator, surface testers, height gauges or micrometers to monitor operations to ensure they meet quality standards.
Accept or reject finished products including tagging or identifying all products and material that fail to meet specifications.
Read, interpret, and follow basic blueprints, diagrams, engineering drawings and other written
instruction. This includes understanding and applying Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerance (GD & T) symbology.
Recommend adjustments to the assembly or production process to improve quality.
Calibrate or verify test instruments.
Adhere to all safety procedures and promote continuous improvement.

Education and Experience (required):
High School diploma or equivalent.
1 year of inspection experience with common hand gages or equivalent.

Education and Experience (preferred):
1 year of experience programing and operating a Direct Computer Controlled (DCC) CMM.

Skills, Knowledge and Abilities (required):
Knowledge of computers and electronics.
Ability to calibrate or verify test instruments and keep detailed records.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to interact across multiple departments.
Proficient computer skills including MS Office.
Ability to analyze and problem solve with attention to detail.

Skills, Knowledge and Abilities (preferred)
Working knowledge and comprehension of quality standards.
American Society for Quality (ASQ) certified.
Ability to work overtime as needed including weekends.

Additional Information:
Direct Reports: None Travel Requirements: 5%
License and Certification Requirements: None

Physical Requirements:
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met to successfully perform the essential functions of the position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. The employee is regularly required to perform physical activities that require significant use of your arms and legs and moving your whole body, such as climbing, lifting, balancing, walking, stooping, standing for extended periods of time and handling of materials. The employee is required to lift up to 50 pounds on a regular basis. The employee is subject to loud noise, dirt, dust, grease, gases and odors and is required to wear personal protective equipment such as safety glasses and ear protection in required area. Typical vision abilities include close up for fine detailed work and
computer work, distance vision and ability to focus. Regular and predictable attendance is required.
