job.title: Machinist Weekend/Swing Shift
job.description:
Machinist Technician – CNC Machinist

Direct Hire | 60 Openings | Ogden, UT

Company: Parker Hannifin – Commercial Flight Controls Division
Location: Ogden, Utah
Employment Type: Direct Hire / Full-Time
Openings: 60
Pay Range: $20–$40/hour, depending on skills and experience
Relocation Assistance: Up to $7,500 gross relocation assistance; approximately $5,000 after taxes
Experience Level: Experienced CNC Machinists Only

Position Overview

Parker Hannifin's Commercial Flight Controls Division is seeking highly skilled and experienced CNC Machinists to join its manufacturing operation in Ogden, Utah. These are direct-hire opportunities supporting the production of precision components for the aerospace industry.

This opportunity is designed for experienced machinists who can do more than simply operate a machine. Successful candidates should be comfortable with machine setup, tooling, offsets, process adjustments, blueprint interpretation, precision inspection, troubleshooting, and machining close-tolerance components with limited supervision.

The ideal candidates will have a strong background in CNC machining, with particular interest in individuals experienced with Swiss lathes, grinding, CNC mills, and/or manual machining. Candidates should be able to independently evaluate machining conditions, troubleshoot production issues, make adjustments, and maintain the quality and efficiency of their work.

This is NOT an Entry-Level Machine Operator Position

We are specifically seeking experienced CNC Machinists who can independently perform complex setups and machining operations.

Strong candidates may have experience with:

  • CNC Swiss lathes
  • CNC turning
  • CNC milling
  • Precision grinding
  • Manual machining
  • Complex machine setups
  • Tight-tolerance aerospace components
  • Tooling and fixture setup
  • CNC offsets and adjustments
  • Process troubleshooting
  • Precision inspection and measurement

Compensation

Desired Pay Range: $20–$40/hour DOE

Compensation will be determined based on the candidate's skills, machining experience, technical capabilities, and overall qualifications.

Important Recruiting Note: Share the $20–$40/hour range with candidates. Do not tell a candidate they are guaranteed a specific hourly rate.

Available Shifts

Weekend Shift

Friday–Sunday | 5:00 AM–5:00 PM

  • 36 hours per week
  • $6/hour shift differential
  • Three-day work schedule

Swing Shift

Monday–Thursday | 3:00 PM–1:30 AM

  • Four-day work schedule
  • Shift differential applies

Candidates should be clearly informed of the schedule and applicable shift differential during the initial conversation.

Relocation Assistance

Relocation assistance is available for qualified candidates relocating to the Ogden, Utah area.

Relocation Assistance: Up to $7,500 gross
Approximate after-tax amount: $5,000

Target Relocation Markets

Prioritize experienced CNC machinists currently located in:

  • Idaho
  • Utah
  • Nevada
  • Arizona
  • Wyoming
  • New Mexico
  • Colorado
  • Montana

Utah candidates: Relocation assistance may be available for candidates living more than 50 miles from Ogden.

Key Benefits

Parker Hannifin offers a comprehensive benefits package, including:

  • Benefits beginning Day 1
  • Up to $10,000 per year in tuition reimbursement
  • Shift differentials for applicable shifts
  • 401(k) vested Day 1
  • 5% company 401(k) match
  • Onsite cafeteria
  • Opportunities for professional development and advancement

Position Responsibilities

The Machinist Technician will set up and operate a variety of conventional and numerically controlled machining centers while working on complex, close-tolerance production components.

CNC Machine Setup & Operation

  • Set up, adjust, and operate CNC and conventional machining equipment.
  • Perform complex setups involving multiple workpiece stations and standard or custom workholding devices.
  • Run multiple machines efficiently, including simultaneous operations when required.
  • Select and install appropriate tooling, fixtures, and workholding.
  • Make necessary machine adjustments and offsets within established procedures.
  • Monitor machining operations and make process adjustments to maintain quality and productivity.
  • Adapt or modify tooling when necessary to achieve required machining results.

Precision Machining

  • Machine components requiring tight dimensional tolerances, complex contours, dimensional relationships, and specific surface-finish requirements.
  • Apply strong knowledge of production machining techniques, tooling, materials, and shop practices.
  • Work with a variety of production machines, materials, tooling, and machining processes.
  • Develop or refine machining processes when documentation is limited.
  • Troubleshoot machining problems and determine appropriate corrective actions.

Blueprint & Engineering Interpretation

  • Read and interpret:
    • Blueprints
    • Complex engineering drawings
    • Engineering specifications
    • Planning sheets
    • Quality requirements
    • Charts and tables
    • Sketches
    • Verbal instructions
  • Understand dimensional requirements, tolerances, surface finishes, and other manufacturing specifications.
  • Identify potential drawing or process issues and communicate them appropriately.

Engineering & Process Support

  • Interface directly with Engineering to resolve drawing discrepancies and manufacturing issues.
  • Recommend potential design or process improvements.
  • Assist Engineering with developing effective manufacturing processes.
  • Provide input regarding tooling requirements and may assist with tooling design.
  • Help identify opportunities to improve production efficiency, quality, and cost.

Quality & Inspection

  • Machine and inspect parts to ensure they meet customer and engineering specifications.
  • Perform in-process and final inspection using precision measuring equipment, including:
    • Calipers
    • Micrometers
    • Precision gauges
    • Comparators
    • Surface plates
    • Other inspection equipment
  • May operate or utilize CMM equipment.
  • Monitor dimensions and tolerances throughout the machining process.
  • Ensure inspection equipment is properly calibrated and used according to requirements.
  • Perform statistical process control (SPC) activities as required.

Equipment Maintenance

  • Routinely maintain machining equipment to support cleanliness, accuracy, reliability, and production performance.
  • Identify equipment issues and troubleshoot problems when appropriate.
  • Maintain tools, fixtures, machines, and work areas in proper operating condition.

Lean Manufacturing & Continuous Improvement

  • Actively participate in Lean manufacturing initiatives.
  • Identify opportunities to improve:
    • Productivity
    • Quality
    • Efficiency
    • Cost
    • Safety
    • Workflow
  • Recommend and implement process improvements within the work area.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives and operational goals.

Team Support & Leadership

  • Work independently with minimal supervision while contributing effectively within a team environment.
  • Help coordinate workload priorities based on business demand.
  • Provide guidance and technical assistance to less-experienced machinists.
  • Train and mentor other team members as needed.
  • Serve as a technical resource within the machining area.

Required Qualifications

Experience

  • 5+ years of directly related machining experience in a high-technology manufacturing environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Strong CNC machining experience is required.
  • Experience with complex machining setups strongly preferred.
  • Aerospace, defense, medical device, or other precision manufacturing experience is highly desirable.

Technical Skills

Candidates should be proficient in several of the following:

  • CNC machining
  • CNC setup
  • CNC turning
  • CNC milling
  • Swiss machining
  • Grinding
  • Manual machining
  • Tooling
  • Fixtures and workholding
  • Machine offsets
  • Process troubleshooting
  • Precision inspection
  • GD&T/tolerancing
  • Blueprint interpretation
  • Shop mathematics
  • Trigonometry
  • SPC
  • Lean manufacturing

Blueprint & Mathematics

  • Ability to read and interpret complex blueprints and engineering drawings.
  • Ability to understand engineering specifications and manufacturing documentation.
  • Working knowledge of advanced shop mathematics.
  • Ability to apply trigonometry when required.
  • Strong understanding of dimensions, tolerances, and precision machining requirements.

Communication & Teamwork

  • Effective verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, and other team members.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a production environment.
  • Strong problem-solving and troubleshooting capabilities.
  • Demonstrated ability to train and mentor less-experienced employees.

Physical & Work Environment

The position requires the ability to:

  • Stand, walk, and sit for extended periods.
  • Use hands and demonstrate strong manual dexterity when operating machinery and handling components.
  • Maintain close visual attention to machining operations and precision measurements.
  • Work safely around CNC machinery, tooling, materials, and production equipment.
  • Lift up to 50 pounds when required.
  • Maintain regular attendance and reliable work performance.
  • Work cooperatively and professionally with other team members.

Reasonable accommodations may be available for qualified individuals to perform the essential functions of the position.

Ideal Candidate Profile

We are looking for a career-level machinist, not someone whose experience is limited to loading and unloading CNC machines.

The strongest candidates will be able to explain:

  • How they perform a CNC setup from start to finish
  • How they select and change tooling
  • How they establish or adjust offsets
  • How they troubleshoot dimensional or machining problems
  • How they read complex blueprints
  • How they inspect precision components
  • How they determine whether a part is within tolerance
  • How they work with Engineering to resolve manufacturing issues
  • What types of CNC equipment they have personally operated
  • Their experience with Swiss lathes, mills, grinders, and manual machines
  • The tightest tolerances and most complex components they have machined

Recruiter Prescreen Questions

Before submitting a candidate, confirm:

  1. How many years of hands-on CNC machining experience do you have?
  2. How much of your experience is as a CNC Machinist versus Machine Operator?
  3. What CNC machines have you personally set up and operated?
  4. Do you have experience with Swiss lathes?
  5. Do you have experience with CNC mills?
  6. Do you have experience with grinding or manual machining?
  7. Can you independently perform a complete CNC setup, including tooling, fixtures, offsets, and adjustments?
  8. What types of materials and components have you machined?
  9. Have you worked with tight-tolerance or precision components? Please provide examples.
  10. Are you comfortable reading complex blueprints and engineering drawings?
  11. What precision measuring equipment have you used?
  12. Do you have experience with CMM, SPC, or other quality-control processes?
  13. Have you worked directly with Engineering to troubleshoot machining or drawing issues?
  14. Are you comfortable working with minimal supervision?
  15. Which shift are you interested in?
  16. Are you open to relocating to Ogden, UT?
  17. If relocating, where are you currently located and approximately how far are you from Ogden?

Sourcing Direction

Please prioritize highly skilled, experienced CNC Machinists over general machine operators.

Do not limit searches to candidates with the exact title "CNC Machinist." Strong candidates may have titles such as:

  • CNC Machinist
  • Senior CNC Machinist
  • CNC Technician
  • Machinist Technician
  • Precision Machinist
  • CNC Setup Machinist
  • Swiss Machinist
  • CNC Mill Machinist
  • CNC Lathe Machinist
  • Manufacturing Machinist
  • Aerospace Machinist
  • Tool & Die Machinist
  • Journeyman Machinist

job.description:

  • Perform mechanical and electrical maintenance and repairs on production machinery and facility support equipment.

  • Identify required parts and maintain current inventories, and parts reorder lists.

job.title: Director of Operations
job.description:
Director of Operations

The Director of Operations will lead the day-to-day operations and financial performance of a manufacturing facility. This highly visible, hands-on leadership role oversees production, maintenance, quality, safety, scheduling, and workforce performance while partnering cross-functionally with Finance, HR, Sales, Customer Service, Supply Chain, and Quality.

The ideal candidate understands that manufacturing performance drives financial performance and will spend significant time on the floor developing leaders, improving processes, solving problems, and driving accountability for results.

Location: Milwaukee, WI
Compensation: $150,000 plus annual bonus

Key Responsibilities

  • P&L & Financial Performance: Own the facility P&L, budget, forecasting, operating costs, labor, overtime, scrap, material usage, maintenance, and profitability. Identify variances and implement corrective actions.
  • Plant Operations: Lead manufacturing operations across all shifts, ensuring staffing, equipment, materials, and scheduling are aligned with customer demand and business objectives.
  • Production Performance: Drive throughput, OEE, efficiency, labor productivity, schedule attainment, capacity utilization, and overall manufacturing performance.
  • Cost & Productivity: Identify opportunities to reduce labor, scrap, material usage, overtime, downtime, and operating expenses while maintaining safety, quality, and customer service.
  • Continuous Improvement: Lead Lean and continuous improvement initiatives focused on productivity, waste reduction, equipment utilization, changeovers, downtime, and capacity.
  • Maintenance & Equipment: Ensure equipment reliability, effective maintenance practices, root-cause resolution, and sound capital investment decisions.
  • Safety & Quality: Establish safety and quality as core operating priorities. Hold leaders accountable for safe work practices, regulatory compliance, quality performance, defect reduction, and corrective actions.
  • Customer & Delivery: Ensure the plant has the capacity and operational discipline to meet customer commitments and improve on-time delivery and schedule reliability.
  • Leadership Development: Lead, coach, and develop the plant's management and supervisory team while building a culture of accountability, engagement, and continuous improvement.
  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Partner with Finance, HR, Sales, Customer Service, Supply Chain, and Quality to align operational decisions with customer and business objectives.
  • Growth & Capacity: Evaluate staffing, equipment, technology, processes, and capacity requirements to support continued growth.
Qualifications
  • Progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
  • Demonstrated plant or location-level P&L, budgeting, forecasting, and cost management experience.
  • Strong knowledge of production management, capacity planning, labor productivity, equipment utilization, quality, maintenance, and manufacturing cost drivers.
  • Experience with Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, root-cause problem solving, and KPI-driven management.
  • Bachelor’s degree in operations, Manufacturing, Engineering, Business, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience may be considered.

job.title: Learning Architect
job.description:
Learning Architect (LA)

Position Overview

The Learning Architect (LA) is responsible for platform-specific curriculum design, development, and ongoing maintenance within the GMQLD operating model. This role partners closely with site Subject Matter Experts (SMEs), Platform Leads, and the Center of Excellence (COE) to ensure learning content remains current, compliant, and aligned with manufacturing processes and business needs.

The ideal candidate brings a strong combination of Learning & Development/instructional design expertise and experience within a GxP-regulated manufacturing environment.

Key Responsibilities

Platform Curriculum Design & Development

  • Design and develop platform-specific training content within COE governance frameworks and global standards.
  • Address approximately 90% platform-level content and 10% site-specific content, as assigned by the M2/P4 Platform Lead.
  • Partner with site SMEs to develop curricula that accurately reflect current manufacturing processes.
  • Apply process-based curriculum principles, organizing learning content by manufacturing process with task-level qualifications.
  • Ensure curricula align with the three-layer content model: Global, Platform, and Site.
  • Leverage global COE content as the foundation for platform-specific curriculum development.

Content Governance & Quality

  • Develop and maintain training content in accordance with COE standards, governance frameworks, quality requirements, and regulatory expectations.
  • Identify content gaps and site-specific needs and escalate them to the Platform Lead and COE for resolution.
  • Support learning equivalency, exception, and substitution decisions in alignment with the Quality system.
  • Ensure learning materials remain current, accurate, compliant, and aligned with manufacturing requirements.

Collaboration & Stakeholder Partnership

  • Partner with the Platform Lead (M2/P4) on Learning & Development strategy and business priorities across platform sites.
  • Interface with the COE to ensure alignment with global standards, governance requirements, and cross-platform initiatives.
  • Collaborate with Learning Execution Partners (LEPs) to understand site-specific execution needs and incorporate feedback into curriculum updates.
  • Work cross-functionally with teams including Quality, Operations, Engineering, and Manufacturing.
  • Represent the platform in cross-functional forums, audits, and governance reviews.
  • Collaborate effectively across multiple sites and time zones.

Continuous Improvement

  • Support Time to Qualification optimization initiatives by identifying training burden, content redundancies, and qualification bottlenecks.
  • Contribute to On-the-Job Training (OJT) standardization across platform sites.
  • Use data and qualification outcomes to identify opportunities to improve curriculum effectiveness.
  • Recommend enhancements to learning content, processes, and qualification programs.

Basic Qualifications

Education

  • Bachelor's degree required; OR
  • Minimum of 10 years of equivalent relevant experience in lieu of a degree.

Experience

  • 5+ years of experience in a GxP-regulated environment.
  • Experience in one or more of the following areas:
    • Learning & Development
    • Instructional Design
    • Manufacturing Operations
    • Quality Operations
  • Experience with curriculum design, Learning Management Systems (LMS), and GMP training requirements.
  • Strong understanding of:
    • GxP requirements
    • Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP)
    • Regulatory requirements
    • Compliance training
  • English proficiency, both written and verbal.

Preferred Skills & Experience

  • Deep knowledge of manufacturing processes such as:
    • Prefilled Syringes (PFS)
    • Cartridge manufacturing
    • DAP/EM
    • Chemical manufacturing
    • Biologics
  • Experience developing process-based or competency-based curriculum architectures.
  • Experience supporting learning programs across multiple manufacturing sites.
  • Strong cross-functional collaboration skills, particularly with Quality, Operations, Engineering, and Manufacturing teams.
  • Experience with digital learning tools and methodologies.
  • Experience with Digital OJT (DOJT), OJT programs, or OJT standardization.
  • Familiarity with Workday, SuccessFactors, or similar HR/Learning Management Systems.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to use data to evaluate training effectiveness and qualification

job.title: Director of Operations
job.description:
Director of Operations
Position Overview

The Director of Operations will lead the day-to-day operations and financial performance of a manufacturing facility. This highly visible, hands-on leadership role oversees production, maintenance, quality, safety, scheduling, and workforce performance while partnering cross-functionally with Finance, HR, Sales, Customer Service, Supply Chain, and Quality.
The ideal candidate understands that manufacturing performance drives financial performance and will spend significant time on the floor developing leaders, improving processes, solving problems, and driving accountability for results.

Location: Albany, NY
Compensation: $150,000 plus annual bonus

Key Responsibilities

  • P&L & Financial Performance: Own the facility P&L, budget, forecasting, operating costs, labor, overtime, scrap, material usage, maintenance, and profitability. Identify variances and implement corrective actions.
  • Plant Operations: Lead manufacturing operations across all shifts, ensuring staffing, equipment, materials, and scheduling are aligned with customer demand and business objectives.
  • Production Performance: Drive throughput, OEE, efficiency, labor productivity, schedule attainment, capacity utilization, and overall manufacturing performance.
  • Cost & Productivity: Identify opportunities to reduce labor, scrap, material usage, overtime, downtime, and operating expenses while maintaining safety, quality, and customer service.
  • Continuous Improvement: Lead Lean and continuous improvement initiatives focused on productivity, waste reduction, equipment utilization, changeovers, downtime, and capacity.
  • Maintenance & Equipment: Ensure equipment reliability, effective maintenance practices, root-cause resolution, and sound capital investment decisions.
  • Safety & Quality: Establish safety and quality as core operating priorities. Hold leaders accountable for safe work practices, regulatory compliance, quality performance, defect reduction, and corrective actions.
  • Customer & Delivery: Ensure the plant has the capacity and operational discipline to meet customer commitments and improve on-time delivery and schedule reliability.
  • Leadership Development: Lead, coach, and develop the plant's management and supervisory team while building a culture of accountability, engagement, and continuous improvement.
  • Cross-Functional Leadership: Partner with Finance, HR, Sales, Customer Service, Supply Chain, and Quality to align operational decisions with customer and business objectives.
  • Growth & Capacity: Evaluate staffing, equipment, technology, processes, and capacity requirements to support continued growth.
Qualifications
  • Progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
  • Demonstrated plant or location-level P&L, budgeting, forecasting, and cost management experience.
  • Strong knowledge of production management, capacity planning, labor productivity, equipment utilization, quality, maintenance, and manufacturing cost drivers.
  • Experience with Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, root-cause problem solving, and KPI-driven management.
  • Bachelor’s degree in operations, Manufacturing, Engineering, Business, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience may be considered.

job.description:
Position Purpose and Objectives

The Accounts Payable / Accounts Receivable Coordinator supports the Finance Department by managing accounts payable and accounts receivable activities, maintaining accurate financial records, processing vendor and customer transactions, monitoring outstanding balances, and assisting with account reconciliations.

Essential Job Functions

Accounts Payable

  • Receive, review, verify, code, and process vendor invoices.
  • Match invoices with purchase orders and supporting documentation, as applicable.
  • Prepare and schedule vendor payments according to established payment terms and company procedures.
  • Research and resolve invoice, purchase order, payment, and credit discrepancies.
  • Reconcile vendor statements and maintain accurate vendor account records.
  • Process employee expense reports and reimbursement requests.
  • Maintain organized and accurate accounts payable records and supporting documentation.
  • Assist with AP-related inquiries from vendors, employees, and internal departments.
  • Ensure invoices and payments are processed accurately and in a timely manner.

Accounts Receivable

  • Prepare and distribute accurate customer invoices in a timely manner.

  • Ability to handle sensitive and confidential financial, customer, vendor, and employee information with discretion.

job.title: Senior Technical Business Analyst
job.description:
Senior Technical Business Analyst

Overview

Client is seeking a highly analytical Senior Technical Business Analyst to support requirements engineering across a complex portfolio of enterprise applications. This role focuses on analyzing existing systems, eliciting and documenting business requirements, identifying business rules and process flows, and translating business needs into structured technical specifications for development teams.

The ideal candidate will collaborate with business stakeholders, architects, developers, compliance teams, and operations teams to ensure solutions are clearly defined, well understood, and ready for implementation within an Agile delivery environment.

Core Responsibilities

• Partner with stakeholders to gather, analyze, document, and validate business requirements, objectives, success criteria, business rules, workflows, and exception scenarios.

• Perform detailed analysis of enterprise applications, integrations, data flows, and technical constraints to identify gaps, enhancements, and process improvement opportunities.

• Create and maintain Functional Requirements Documents (FRDs), feature specifications, user stories, acceptance criteria, and other requirements artifacts.

• Develop requirements using structured methodologies, including GIVEN/WHEN/THEN (BDD) approaches when appropriate.

• Create process flows, decision trees, system interaction diagrams, state diagrams, and data models to document end-to-end business processes and system interactions.

• Collaborate with architects and technical teams to document APIs, integrations, data contracts, interface requirements, data mappings, and transformation rules.

• Facilitate requirement reviews, walkthroughs, and clarification sessions while serving as a liaison between business and technical teams.

• Support backlog refinement, sprint planning, Agile ceremonies, User Acceptance Testing (UAT), and solution validation activities.

• Proactively identify risks, dependencies, edge cases, exception scenarios, and error-handling requirements throughout the delivery lifecycle.

Essential Qualifications, Skills, and Technologies

• 5–10+ years of experience as a Technical Business Analyst, Systems Analyst, or Business Systems Analyst in software engineering environments.

• Proven experience working on complex enterprise applications and system integrations.

• Strong requirements elicitation, analysis, documentation, validation, and requirements management skills.

• Experience creating functional specifications, user stories, process flows, acceptance criteria, and other technical documentation.

• Strong understanding of APIs, REST services, JSON payloads, integration patterns, and data structures.

• Working knowledge of relational databases, SQL queries, and data mapping concepts.

• Ability to analyze technical artifacts and communicate findings effectively to both technical and non-technical audiences.

• Experience working within Agile and Scrum delivery environments.

• Proficiency with Jira, Confluence, Azure DevOps, or similar collaboration and delivery tools.

• Strong stakeholder management, facilitation, written communication, and verbal communication skills.

• Ability to translate business needs into technical requirements and technical concepts into business language.

Preferred Skills or Experience

• Financial Services or Banking industry experience.

• Experience in Wealth Management, Digital Banking, or Financial Technology platforms.

• Familiarity with Markdown documentation standards.

• Experience with Mermaid.js, Miro, Visio, or other diagramming tools.

• Knowledge of Behavior-Driven Development (BDD) methodologies.

• Experience establishing and enforcing Definition of Ready (DoR) standards.

• Experience performing application audits, reverse engineering business logic, and documenting legacy systems with limited existing documentation.

Work Details

Remote

job.title: Head of Product - Commercial Lending
job.description:
Head of Product – Commercial Lending Technology

Location: Remote – United States
Employment Type: Full-Tim

The Opportunity

We are seeking a senior Product leader with deep commercial lending and LOS experience to help shape and build the next generation of a commercial lending platform. This person will own product strategy and roadmap priorities, bring strong knowledge of the full commercial lending lifecycle, and work closely with Engineering to turn market and business needs into scalable product capabilities. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who can set direction, understand the competitive landscape, and stay close to the details as the product is built.

 

What You'll Do

  • Own the product strategy, roadmap, and prioritization for a commercial lending technology platform.
  • Bring deep commercial lending expertise across origination, underwriting, credit approval, monitoring, and portfolio management.
  • Use market trends, competitive intelligence, customer needs, and business priorities to guide product decisions.
  • Translate lending workflows and business requirements into clear product requirements, acceptance criteria, and development priorities.
  • Partner closely with Engineering throughout planning, development, testing, and release.
  • Lead and develop a small Product team while remaining hands-on in the day-to-day work.
  • Help establish practical Product processes around requirements, roadmap management, prioritization, and product validation.
  • Identify opportunities to improve workflows, reduce manual effort, and create stronger differentiation in the commercial lending market.
  • Participate in customer or prospect conversations when Product expertise is needed.

What We're Looking For

Required Experience

  • Significant Product Management experience within commercial lending technology, commercial loan origination systems, banking technology, or a closely related fintech environment.
  • Deep knowledge of the end-to-end commercial lending lifecycle.
  • Experience owning a commercial lending product, product line, or significant product portfolio.
  • Previous leadership responsibility for Product professionals or a Product function.
  • Demonstrated experience owning product strategy, roadmaps, and prioritization.
  • Ability to understand market dynamics and competitive positioning within lending technology.
  • Experience translating business requirements and complex financial workflows into scalable software capabilities.
  • Strong history of partnering directly with Software Engineering teams.
  • Ability to balance strategic thinking with detailed, hands-on Product work.
  • Strong written, verbal, and executive communication skills.

Preferred Experience

  • Experience working directly for a commercial LOS, lending software, banking technology, or fintech provider.
  • Product experience involving commercial credit underwriting, financial spreading, credit decisioning, portfolio management, or loan workflow technology.
  • Experience building or launching a new product or substantial new platform capability.
  • Familiarity with APIs, integrations, bank cores, and third-party financial technology.
  • Experience introducing stronger Product processes within a smaller or growing software organization.
  • Experience working in an entrepreneurial environment where priorities can change quickly and leaders wear multiple hats.

Work Environment

  • Remote position within the United States
  • Candidates should be comfortable maintaining meaningful overlap with Pacific Time business hours
  • Limited travel expected, primarily for occasional company meetings or strategic in-person sessions
  • Small, distributed Product and Engineering organization
  • Highly collaborative environment with direct access to company leadership

Why This Opportunity

This is an opportunity to have a meaningful influence on the development of a commercial lending product rather than simply inherit and maintain an established roadmap.
The person selected will bring commercial lending knowledge that is critical to the next phase of the platform, helping determine what gets built, how the product should compete, and how technology can improve the commercial lending process.
For someone who understands commercial lending deeply and enjoys building products in a smaller, hands-on environment, this role offers significant ownership and visibility.

job.title: Project Controls Specialist - (Oil/Gas)
job.description:
BASIC FUNCTION:
Supports project team by providing financial controls and tracking for regional capital projects, and project manager with management tools, controls, and analysis, allowing manager to make informed decisions with accurate and timely data.

ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES/RESPONSIBILITIES: (functions considered essential as defined by ADA)
Leads in the overall project cost and schedule control efforts during capital efforts
Initiates correct structuring setups to facilitate data collection and control monitoring during the execution process
Tracks contractor performance, processes payments and logistics
Tracks and forecasts costs throughout life of the project
Tracks progress against budget throughout year
Sets safety example by keeping current on LRST and other safety initiatives within the plans

Special assignments or tasks assigned to the employee by their superior, as determined from time to time in their sole and complete discretion.

EXPERIENCE:
A minimum of 5 years in planning, estimating, and construction/maintenance management in a process plant environment is required.

EDUCATIONAL LEVEL:
A minimum of a High School Diploma or equivalent is required.

PREFERRED EDUCATIONAL LEVEL:
A Bachelor's Degree in Engineering or other technical discipline is preferred.

REQUIRED SKILLS:
Broad understanding of engineering, construction, logistics and financial processes. Advanced knowledge of accounting, contracting, and procurement software systems and processes. Spreadsheet software skills. Ability to work in a fast paced work environment and deliver to required deadlines. Ability to work additional hours as required to support project control efforts. Prioritization skills are required. Ability to see how all the pieces affect the overall refinery, i.e., big picture perspective. Ability to effectively communicate with others, both written and verbal communication. Advanced reading and writing skills, with the ability to perform intermediate mathematical calculations.

PREFERRED SKILLS:
General proficiency in Microsoft packages Word, Outlook, Excel, Project, Access as well as Primavera (P6) etc. General knowledge of procedures and practices for contracting field construction activities are preferred.

SUPERVISORY/MANAGERIAL RESPONSIBILITIES:
None.

WORK CONDITIONS:
Office based with up to 5% travel by land and air required. Petroleum refinery, warehouse/plant environment including but not limited to chemicals, pressure vessels tanks, rotating equipment, loud noise and vibrations. Subject to all temperatures, weather and varying road conditions.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
Job conditions require sitting, talking or hearing, making precise hand and finger movements, reaching or grasping, perceiving color difference, and wearing personal protective equipment (beards not permitted). Job conditions may require standing, walking, making visual inspections, lifting and/or carrying up to 10lbs, and ability to operate and drive all assigned company vehicles at company standard insurance rates is essential, valid state drivers license and proof of insurance required.

ENVIRONMENTAL, HEALTH, & SAFETY RESPONSIBILITIES:
Our primary values are: We put health and safety first; We care about the environment.
All employees are expected to work safely every day and be safety & environmental leaders. This includes active participation in the following:
Stops and/or reports any unsafe work or conditions
Follows safety & environmental policies and procedures
Supports safety & environmental goals and initiatives
Participates in safety & environmental meetings, training, emergency drills and hazard recognition programs
Reports all accidents, injuries and near misses, and participates in associated investigations
Participates in industrial hygiene, medical surveillance and behavior based safety programs

job.title: Product Manager/Product Owner – Customer Communications
job.description:
Product Manager / Product Owner – Customer Experience & Communications

Location: New York, NY
Work Arrangement: Hybrid – 3 days per week in the office during training; after training, in-office as needed
Schedule: Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM–5:00 PM EST
Employment Type: 6-Month Contract with Potential for FTE Conversion
Openings: 2
Compensation: $65–$85/hour
Start Date: ASAP

Position Overview

We are seeking two Product Managers / Product Owners to support customer experience, digital transformation, and customer communications initiatives for a complex, customer-facing organization.

This role combines Product Ownership, Project Management, and Business Analysis responsibilities. The ideal candidate will be comfortable working in an Agile environment, managing product backlogs, gathering and translating business requirements, coordinating development activities, and working closely with business stakeholders, technology teams, and third-party vendors.

The team supports digital customer experiences and multi-channel communications across platforms such as websites, mobile applications, SMS, email, voice, and other customer-facing channels. The position will also support transformational initiatives and time-sensitive customer communications, including emergency and weather-related notifications.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage and prioritize product and program backlogs, enhancements, features, epics, and user stories.

  • Partner with business stakeholders to understand customer and business needs and translate them into actionable requirements.

  • Develop clear, concise user stories, acceptance criteria, business requirements, and functional specifications.

  • Support product and feature development across digital customer channels, including websites, mobile applications, and other customer-facing platforms.

  • Lead or support Agile ceremonies including sprint planning, stand-ups, backlog refinement/grooming, reviews, retrospectives, and release planning.

  • Coordinate Agile teams or pods from a business and product perspective.

  • Track sprint and release progress, team velocity, deliverables, risks, issues, and dependencies.

  • Manage project plans, schedules, action items, status reporting, documentation, and other program materials.

  • Coordinate with technology teams, vendors, and internal stakeholders to ensure requirements and deliverables remain on track.

  • Conduct requirements analysis, process analysis, testing, UAT, and issue resolution.

  • Develop test plans and test cases and coordinate testing activities with business and technical teams.

  • Support customer communications across multiple channels, including SMS, email, voice, web, and mobile.

  • Support customer communications during emergency or time-sensitive situations.

  • Identify opportunities to improve product processes, governance, intake, and overall customer experience.

  • Conduct research and analysis related to digital customer experience, industry trends, customer behavior, and emerging technologies.

  • Prepare presentations, status reports, and documentation for management and other stakeholders.

  • Manage multiple priorities and workstreams in a fast-paced, sometimes ambiguous environment.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree required.

  • 3+ years of experience in Product Management, Product Ownership, Project Management, Business Analysis, Customer Experience, or a related discipline.

  • Demonstrated experience working in an Agile product development environment.

  • Experience managing or supporting product backlogs, requirements, user stories, and feature prioritization.

  • Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.

  • Ability to work effectively with both technical and non-technical teams.

  • Experience coordinating projects, deliverables, risks, issues, and competing priorities.

  • Strong analytical, organizational, documentation, and problem-solving skills.

  • Experience with Microsoft Office applications, including Excel.

  • Technical aptitude and ability to quickly understand business processes, technology platforms, and systems.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability to work independently and effectively within a small, complex team.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience as a Product Owner for an Agile development team.

  • Experience with SAFe Agile, Agile transformation, or large-scale Agile programs.

  • Experience with digital customer experience, websites, mobile applications, or digital products.

  • Experience with customer communications or multi-channel communication platforms.

  • Experience with SMS, email, voice, web, mobile, or other customer communication technologies.

  • Vendor management or third-party technology partner experience.

  • Experience with Azure DevOps, Monday.com, Jira, or similar Agile/product management tools.

  • Experience with web accessibility guidelines and compliance.

  • Experience in the utility industry or another regulated/highly complex environment.

  • Knowledge of customer operations, customer assistance programs, or customer-facing regulations.

  • Experience supporting emergency communications or other time-sensitive customer initiatives.

  • Experience preparing executive, regulatory, or formal stakeholder presentations and documentation.

Additional Information

This is a 6-month contract opportunity with potential for conversion to a full-time position based on performance and business needs.

Candidates should be comfortable working in a hybrid environment in New York City. A valid driver's license may be required for potential FTE conversion; driving is not required as part of the day-to-day responsibilities of this position.

Facilities Maintenance Technician – HVAC Experience

Location: Chandler, AZ
Employment Type: Full-Time | Onsite
Pay Range: $30–$45+/hr DOE

Position Overview

Advanced manufacturing facility seeking a Facilities Maintenance Technician to maintain building infrastructure, facility equipment, and utilities. This is primarily a facilities maintenance role with approximately 20% HVAC responsibilities. The ideal candidate will have strong mechanical/electrical troubleshooting skills with commercial HVAC experience.

Key Responsibilities

  • Perform preventive and corrective maintenance on facility systems, building equipment, and infrastructure.
  • Troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and general building maintenance issues.
  • Support commercial HVAC systems including RTUs, AHUs, exhaust systems, and split systems.
  • Coordinate with contractors/vendors and maintain work orders, PM records, and parts inventory.
  • Respond to facility breakdowns and emergencies while following LOTO, OSHA, and site safety procedures.

Qualifications

  • 5+ years of facilities, industrial, commercial, or building maintenance experience.
  • Must have EPA Certification
  • Strong mechanical and electrical troubleshooting skills.
  • Commercial HVAC experience preferred; experience with RTUs, AHUs, ventilation, or split systems a plus.
  • Familiarity with motors, pumps, compressors, VFDs, controls, and electrical schematics.
  • Manufacturing, industrial, aerospace, semiconductor, or large commercial facility experience preferred.

Work Environment

  • Large advanced manufacturing facility with mechanical rooms, rooftops, and production areas.
  • Frequent standing, walking, climbing ladders, and accessing equipment.
  • May work around industrial machinery, utilities, and facility systems.
  • Overtime and occasional emergency response may be required.
  • Must follow all site-specific safety and PPE requirements.

Compensation & Benefits

$35–$45+/hr DOE

Medical, dental, vision, 401(k), paid time off, and career growth opportunities.

job.title: Payroll Clerk
job.description:
Payroll Clerk

Location: South Bend, IN
Schedule: Monday–Friday, 8:00 AM–5:00 PM
Work Arrangement: 100% Onsite
Employment Type: Temp-to-Hire

Position Overview

The Payroll Clerk is responsible for supporting all functions of the time and attendance payroll system for a union workforce. This position ensures accurate payroll processing through the reconciliation of employee hours, incentive pay, and production data. The Payroll Clerk will partner closely with Human Resources, supervisors, and operations to ensure payroll activities comply with union agreements, employment policies, and benefits practices.

Key Responsibilities

  • Manage daily payroll operations within ADP eTime, including entering, reviewing, and clearing timecard exceptions.
  • Collaborate with supervisors and employees to verify hours, production data, and incentive pay for payroll accuracy.
  • Reconcile daily payroll and production summaries, ensuring alignment between timekeeping and manufacturing systems.
  • Enter and maintain production data within time and attendance and manufacturing systems.
  • Prepare shift summaries and maintain detailed spreadsheets to support operational planning.
  • Track, document, and process payroll adjustments using supervisor-approved documentation.
  • Research and resolve payroll discrepancies and respond to employee inquiries regarding timecards, pay, and adjustments.
  • Partner with Human Resources to ensure payroll processing adheres to union contracts, policies, and benefits practices.
  • Maintain accurate tracking and reconciliation of union dues payments.
  • Conduct payroll audits to ensure accuracy, compliance, and process integrity.
  • Support process improvement initiatives between operations and payroll to improve efficiency and accuracy.
  • Train and support team members on payroll processes and system usage.
  • Generate and distribute payroll and operational reports as needed.
  • Document internal payroll processes and maintain organized records.
  • Perform additional administrative duties, including label printing, static record reviews, and other assigned tasks.
  • Assist with basic accounting-related tasks as needed.

Skills & Experience

  • 1+ years of experience with ADP eTime or a similar payroll/timekeeping system.
  • 1+ years of experience working in a union environment.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel, including data tracking, reconciliation, and reporting.
  • Strong attention to detail with experience managing and reconciling spreadsheet-based data.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet daily deadlines in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to independently identify and resolve discrepancies.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills with employees, supervisors, and cross-functional teams.
  • Experience within a manufacturing environment preferred.
  • Exposure to SAP preferred.

Education

  • High School Diploma or equivalent required.
  • Some college coursework in Accounting, Business, or a related field preferred.

job.description:
Title: Facility/Site Supervisor (Coyanosa Thermal Treatment Facility)

The Facility/Site Supervisor at the Coyanosa Facility is a critical and dynamic role. Coyanosa TTF is one of the most regulated facilities in SLB. The Facility/Site Supervisor is responsible for working with management to ensure the execution of SLB standards and policies for the facility as they pertain to the regulatory Compliance program, facility sustainment and maintenance, facility administration, and personnel. The Coyanosa Facility Supervisor function is critical in establishing, monitoring, and continuously improving environmental performance and environmental programs at the highly regulated Coyanosa Thermal Treatment Center.

General Duties Include but are not limited to:
• Work with Regulatory Compliance to maintain up-to-date knowledge of laws and regulations affecting local operations.
• Coordinate with Regulatory Compliance for the gathering and submission processes for regulatory licenses and permits.
• Maintain regulatory compliance documentation.
• Support the preparation of reports to management and to regulatory bodies within set time targets.
• Coordinate with Management to Implement procedural modifications based on changes in local laws and regulations.
• Report regulatory compliance incidents to Management and in QUEST.
• Participate in external and internal regulatory audits and inspections and ensure all remedial actions are documented and closed in a timely manner.
• Advise management on corrective actions required.
• Help develop and provide awareness training to employees on processes for internal and external regulatory compliance requirements.

Specific Environmental Duties
• Liaise with local contractors and agencies regarding environmental programs.
• Assess local environmental risks and develop risk controls.
• Coordinate with Management and HSE to recommend changes to environmental procedures, work instructions and checklists as required.
Monitor plans defining how the environmental aspects of the HSE Management System are implemented at the location level. Monitor and recommended improvements.
• Ensure compliance to Environmental policies, standards and procedures.
• Plan and assist in compliance audits and self-audits. Advise management on corrective action required.
• Coordinate environmental training of personnel, including contractors.
• Keep abreast of new documentation and training material related to environmental management and inform management accordingly.
• Ensure that environmental documentation is updated and available on site.
• Advise management on the compliance of the local environmental program with ***, local and national requirements, and regulations.
• Support line management in investigations of environmental incidents.
• Maintain a high level of awareness among personnel through communications, training and promoting active involvement in environmental programs.

Specific Business/Operational Duties
• Implement best practices in facility operations to ensure a consistent professional image for the facility.
• Supervise local staff to optimize process and maximize efficiency.
• Ensure local Staff meet the *** standards, as well as the local, state, and federal regulatory requirements to ensure business continuity and safety.
• Implement quality control programs using LEAN methodology to standardize and optimize facility performance in line with the Global Facility Management strategy.

Onsite Explosive Safety Officer
• Ensure that possessed explosives are authorized by the license.
• Ensure that users of explosives are authorized by the license and are properly trained.
• Ensure that inventories of explosives are completed.
• Ensure that all explosives are stored in a storage facility appropriate for the type of material.
• Ensure that all explosives are properly transported.
• Complete a self-assessment of the facilities at least bi-annually.
• Maintain the records required, as detailed in STD 19 B.O.O.K.
• Implement all other components of the *** Explosives Safety Program not specifically mentioned above.
• Provide emergency and technical assistance, as needed.

o Minimum 1 year in environmental waste

Regulatory Frameworks & Standards

job.description:
Job Title: Sr. Metrology Engineer II
Onsite: Harrodsburg, KY

As part of the Division Quality - Metrology group, to lead metrology tech transfer from R&D to production lines, and provide leadership in problem solving and technical expertise in metrology area.

Lead metrology projects from concept through implementation to support R&D-to-manufacturing transfer and production readiness, including metrology planning, gauge development, system qualification, deployment, and production release.
Collaborate closely with cross-functional teams including QA, engineering, manufacturing, software and controls teams to implement robust measurement solutions.
Develop metrology strategies in terms of gauges capability, capacity, lead time, and cost evaluation, etc.

Survey, develop, deploy and qualify new capable gauges, and measurement systems to meet the new test requirements relating to critical product characteristics including glass defects, glass size, weight, reliability, optical performance, mechanical characteristics, and other critical product attributes.

Design, improve, and validate new test methods using existing metrology systems. Support the design and development of fixtures and tools used in metrology systems.
Develop measurement data reporting, traceability, usability, data analysis applications when deploying new gauges or new test methods and continue improvement afterwards. Partner with controls and software engineers to develop operator interfaces, data collection systems, and databases that support effective use of measurement systems.
Documentations on gauges' engineering or operational work instructions; summarize measurement systems development and qualification reports.

Train users and provide technical support for deployed metrology systems.
Provide metrology technical leadership in 2nd-level troubleshooting metrology issues, performing root cause analysis, and implementing sustainable corrective actions for plant gauges.

Metrology governance - Lead and drive gauge alignment, and metrology standardization including MSA across internal plants, contract manufacturers, and customer sites as needed.
Evaluate current gauge capability and capacity, and drive continuous improvement, governance, and long-term metrology capability development

Education Required:
BS or Higher; Master is preferred. majors in Metrology, Precise Instruments, Optics, Machine Vision, Physics, Materials and Science, Automation and Mechanical Engineering, related

Required Skills:
Knowledge of metrology – calibration traceability, data uncertainty, gauge qualification types, etc.
Knowledge of MSA
Familiar with MS office tools
Familiar with Minitab/Origin
Familiar with Matlab/Python
Basic statistics and reporting capability
Good communication skills
Familiar with Machine Vision is a plus

Working experience in a test lab or glass defects inspection system development is a plus
5% Domestic travel depending on projects stage and schedule to ***, NY
40 hrs/week, expected to work hours required to successfully deliver project and support requirements.

job.title: Contract Site Reliability Engineer
job.description:
Contract Site Reliability Engineer

Overview Client is seeking a Contract Site Reliability Engineer to support its Model Operations and Deployment Engineering team. This role focuses on maintaining, enhancing, and evolving Kubernetes platforms that enable scientific and engineering teams to deploy, operate, and scale critical applications across on-premises and cloud environments.

The ideal candidate will bring strong experience in Kubernetes operations, Linux systems administration, Rancher-based cluster management, infrastructure automation, and GitOps practices. This position will play a key role in improving platform reliability, operational efficiency, and automation across the environment.

Core Responsibilities Maintain and enhance Kubernetes platforms across on-premises and cloud environments to ensure reliability, scalability, and operational efficiency. Support provisioning, upgrades, troubleshooting, and lifecycle management of Kubernetes clusters managed through Rancher. Provide advanced Linux systems administration, including troubleshooting, performance tuning, automation, and operational support. Develop and maintain infrastructure-as-code solutions to standardize and automate platform deployment and management. Support and improve GitOps workflows using ArgoCD for consistent and auditable cluster and application configuration management. Collaborate with developers, scientists, and infrastructure teams to deliver reliable platform services and sustainable engineering solutions. Identify and implement improvements for platform resilience, observability, security, and maintainability through automation and modern SRE practices.

Essential Qualifications, Skills, and Technologies BS in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Information Technology, or a related field preferred, or equivalent professional experience. Minimum 5 years of professional experience in Site Reliability Engineering, Platform Engineering, DevOps, or Systems Engineering roles. Hands-on experience operating and supporting Kubernetes platforms in production environments. Strong experience managing Kubernetes clusters in both on-premises and cloud-based environments. Minimum 5 years of Linux systems administration experience, including troubleshooting, scripting, networking, and performance analysis. Experience with Rancher for Kubernetes cluster management and platform operations. Strong experience implementing infrastructure-as-code solutions for platform provisioning and lifecycle management. Experience with Kubernetes cluster operations, upgrades, networking, storage, troubleshooting, and workload support. Experience with GitOps practices, ArgoCD, Git version control, and deployment automation. Proficiency in Bash, Python, or similar scripting languages for automation and operational tooling. Demonstrated success working within Agile environments, including Scrum or Kanban teams.

Preferred Skills or Experience Experience with hybrid infrastructure environments spanning on-premises and public cloud platforms such as AWS, Azure, or GCP. Experience with Kubernetes observability, logging, monitoring, and alerting tools. Familiarity with Kubernetes and Linux security best practices. Experience supporting scientific research environments, high-performance computing, or computational science workloads. Experience with Cluster API (CAPI)-based infrastructure automation approaches. Knowledge of CI/CD pipeline development and platform automation patterns.

Work Details Remote position. Candidates may reside anywhere within the United States. Must be available to work 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM EST or 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM EST. Contract assignment with an initial duration of 6 months. Potential extension based on business needs. Interview process includes a Teams interview with the hiring manager followed by a Teams interview with additional team members.

job.title: Microsoft 365 Migration Engineer
job.description:
Nesco Data Center is searching for a Senior Microsoft Delivery Engineer & Consultant.

Microsoft 365 Migration Engineer

Job Summary

We are seeking an experienced Microsoft 365 Migration Engineer to lead and execute complex Microsoft 365 cloud migration and implementation projects. This position requires a highly technical engineer with hands-on experience designing, configuring, migrating, troubleshooting, and validating Microsoft 365 environments across multiple workloads.

The successful candidate will be capable of taking an existing Microsoft 365, Microsoft Exchange, Google Workspace, or other email/file collaboration environment and successfully transitioning users and services into a properly architected Microsoft 365 environment.

This is not simply a Microsoft 365 administration role. The ideal candidate has demonstrated experience performing actual production migrations, including tenant-to-tenant migrations, Exchange hybrid migrations, Google Workspace-to-Microsoft 365 migrations, domain and DNS cutovers, identity synchronization, mail-flow changes, Teams migrations, SharePoint migrations, OneDrive migrations, security configuration, and post-migration troubleshooting.

The engineer will work directly with technical stakeholders and client IT teams, provide technical guidance, perform discovery and assessment, execute migration waves and cutovers, troubleshoot issues, and provide documentation and knowledge transfer at project completion.

Core Responsibilities

Microsoft 365 Tenant Architecture & Implementation

  • Architect, configure, validate, and implement Microsoft 365 tenants.

  • Configure Microsoft 365 licensing based on user requirements and licensing strategy.

  • Provision and configure user accounts, mailboxes, groups, and other required Microsoft 365 services.

  • Evaluate existing environments and determine migration dependencies, prerequisites, and risks.

  • Validate Microsoft 365 configuration against security and operational best practices.

  • Support Microsoft 365 Business Premium, Enterprise E3, and Enterprise E5 environments.

  • Understand the capabilities and licensing implications associated with Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, OneDrive for Business, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Entra ID, Defender, and related Microsoft cloud services.

Identity & Authentication

  • Design and implement identity integration between on-premises Active Directory and Microsoft 365.

  • Configure and troubleshoot directory synchronization.

  • Configure, upgrade, and troubleshoot Microsoft Entra Connect / Azure AD Connect environments.

  • Implement and validate Single Sign-On and Pass-through Authentication where required.

  • Perform account matching and synchronization between existing Active Directory accounts and cloud identities.

  • Configure Microsoft Entra ID identity services in cloud-only environments.

  • Configure and troubleshoot Multifactor Authentication.

  • Implement Conditional Access policies and/or Microsoft Security Defaults.

  • Configure self-service password reset and account unlock functionality where required.

  • Troubleshoot identity synchronization, authentication, credential, and access issues.

Exchange Online & Email Security

  • Design and implement Exchange Online environments.

  • Configure and troubleshoot Exchange Online Protection.

  • Configure and validate:

    • SPF

    • DKIM

    • DMARC / anti-spoofing concepts

    • Anti-malware

    • Anti-phishing

    • Safe Links

    • Safe Attachments

    • Spoof intelligence

    • Email encryption

    • Data Loss Prevention policies

  • Configure mail-flow rules and routing.

  • Integrate Microsoft 365 with third-party email security/filtering platforms when required.

  • Troubleshoot inbound and outbound mail-flow issues.

  • Validate DNS records and mail-flow dependencies.

  • Understand SMTP relay requirements for applications, multifunction devices, and other infrastructure.

Exchange Migration

The engineer must have hands-on experience executing production Exchange migrations using one or more migration methodologies, including:

  • Exchange hybrid migrations.

  • On-premises Exchange to Exchange Online.

  • Google Workspace to Microsoft 365.

  • Third-party email platform to Microsoft 365.

  • Microsoft 365 tenant-to-tenant migrations.

  • Mailbox migrations involving:

    • User mailboxes

    • Shared mailboxes

    • Resource mailboxes

    • Public folders

  • Migration of email, calendars, contacts, journals, notes, and other supported mailbox content.

  • Test/pilot migrations.

  • Migration-wave planning and execution.

  • Delta synchronization.

  • Cutover planning and execution.

  • Post-cutover validation.

  • Mail-flow modification.

  • Outlook client connectivity troubleshooting.

  • Migration-related user provisioning and troubleshooting.

Exchange Hybrid Engineering

For environments requiring hybrid Exchange architecture, the engineer should be capable of:

  • Assessing Exchange prerequisites for hybrid deployment.

  • Validating Exchange versions, service packs, and cumulative updates.

  • Validating DNS and Autodiscover functionality.

  • Implementing Exchange hybrid architecture.

  • Configuring coexistence between on-premises Exchange and Exchange Online.

  • Troubleshooting hybrid connectivity.

  • Supporting SMTP relay requirements.

  • Supporting Exchange management requirements after migration.

  • Assisting with legacy Exchange decommissioning when appropriate.

Experience with maintaining an on-premises Exchange server for hybrid management, SMTP relay, or coexistence is highly desirable.

Microsoft 365 Tenant-to-Tenant Migration

The engineer must understand the complexities associated with tenant-to-tenant migrations and be able to coordinate the migration of multiple Microsoft 365 workloads.

Responsibilities may include:

  • Source and destination tenant assessment.

  • Domain and DNS planning.

  • User and identity mapping.

  • Mailbox migration.

  • Teams migration.

  • SharePoint migration.

  • OneDrive migration.

  • Data and permissions validation.

  • Migration-wave planning.

  • Test migrations.

  • Cutover planning.

  • Final synchronization/delta migration.

  • Domain removal and registration during cutover.

  • DNS and FQDN modifications.

  • Post-cutover troubleshooting.

The engineer must understand that tenant-to-tenant migration may require coordinated cutover of Exchange Online, Teams, OneDrive, and SharePoint Online and must be capable of managing the dependencies between these workloads.

Microsoft Teams

  • Design and implement Microsoft Teams environments.

  • Establish Teams governance standards.

  • Configure Teams naming conventions.

  • Establish Teams creation and administrative processes.

  • Configure guest access and external communication policies.

  • Establish approved application/integration standards.

  • Address Teams data security requirements.

  • Configure expiration, retention, and archiving policies.

  • Control Microsoft 365 Group and Teams creation.

  • Build and configure Teams for architectural validation and knowledge transfer.

  • Migrate Teams, channels, and associated files where applicable.

  • Troubleshoot Teams and collaboration migration issues.

  • Understand limitations surrounding private chats, meeting history, participant acceptance, and other non-migratable content.

The engineer should be comfortable working with both the technical implementation and governance side of Microsoft Teams, rather than simply provisioning Teams for users.

SharePoint Online

  • Design and configure SharePoint Online environments.

  • Configure SharePoint Online document libraries.

  • Perform discovery of existing file-server and SharePoint environments.

  • Identify migration dependencies and compatibility issues.

  • Configure and validate SharePoint migration toolsets.

  • Migrate folders, files, shares, sites, and associated data.

  • Execute multiple migration passes to capture changes.

  • Maintain file and folder hierarchies where technically possible.

  • Preserve permissions and access structures where possible.

  • Coordinate SharePoint cutovers.

  • Troubleshoot file naming, invalid-character, embedded URL, permissions, metadata, and other migration issues.

Candidates should understand common SharePoint migration limitations and be able to identify and remediate problematic data before migration.

OneDrive for Business

  • Configure OneDrive for Business for users.

  • Assess existing user home directories and file structures.

  • Identify compatibility and migration issues.

  • Configure and validate OneDrive migration toolsets.

  • Migrate user data from file servers, Google Drive, or another Microsoft 365 tenant.

  • Preserve folder structures, permissions, sharing relationships, and data integrity where possible.

  • Perform test migrations and multiple synchronization passes.

  • Support migration waves and final cutover.

  • Troubleshoot OneDrive migration problems involving:

    • Invalid characters

    • File naming restrictions

    • Embedded URLs

    • Metadata

    • Version history

    • Permissions

    • Shared links

    • Shared folders

Experience with Group Policy and home-directory redirection to OneDrive is preferred.

Microsoft 365 Backup

  • Deploy and configure Microsoft 365 backup solutions.

  • Protect:

    • Exchange Online

    • SharePoint Online

    • OneDrive

    • Teams

    • Microsoft 365 Groups

    • Calendars

    • Tasks

    • Attachments

  • Configure retention policies.

  • Validate recurring backup operations.

  • Perform restore testing and validation where applicable.

  • Ensure administrative access and operational knowledge is transferred to the customer IT team.

Migration Planning & Cutover

The engineer will be responsible for helping plan and execute technically complex migration events with minimal disruption to users.

Responsibilities include:

  • Developing migration plans and technical runbooks.

  • Performing discovery and prerequisite validation.

  • Developing pilot/test migrations.

  • Establishing migration waves.

  • Monitoring migration progress.

  • Troubleshooting migration failures.

  • Coordinating DNS and domain changes.

  • Coordinating mail-flow changes.

  • Performing final synchronization/delta migrations.

  • Executing production cutovers.

  • Validating user access following migration.

  • Performing post-migration cleanup.

  • Supporting users and client IT teams following cutover.

  • Identifying and documenting risks before production migration.

The engineer must understand that migration success involves much more than copying data; it requires careful coordination of identity, authentication, DNS, mail flow, security, client connectivity, permissions, applications, and user access.

Troubleshooting & Technical Support

The engineer must be comfortable troubleshooting complex issues across the Microsoft cloud ecosystem, including:

  • Authentication failures

  • Directory synchronization issues

  • MFA problems

  • Conditional Access issues

  • Exchange Online connectivity

  • Mail-flow failures

  • DNS problems

  • SPF/DKIM/anti-spam configuration

  • Outlook connectivity

  • Hybrid Exchange connectivity

  • Mailbox migration failures

  • Teams access and migration issues

  • SharePoint permissions

  • OneDrive synchronization

  • File migration errors

  • Data integrity issues

  • Permission and access problems

  • Microsoft 365 licensing issues

The engineer must be capable of independently diagnosing problems rather than relying exclusively on escalation to Microsoft or another third party.

Documentation & Knowledge Transfer

  • Create comprehensive technical documentation.

  • Document the final Microsoft 365 architecture and configuration.

  • Document identity and authentication architecture.

  • Document security configurations.

  • Document migration procedures and results.

  • Document administrative procedures and management best practices.

  • Create technical runbooks and operational procedures.

  • Conduct administrator training.

  • Conduct train-the-trainer sessions for client IT personnel.

  • Explain configuration decisions and operational considerations to technical stakeholders.

  • Provide sufficient knowledge transfer for the client's IT team to independently manage the environment following project completion.

Documentation and administrative training are core project deliverables, not secondary responsibilities.

Required Professional Experience

Minimum Qualifications

  • 5+ years of hands-on Microsoft infrastructure/cloud engineering experience.

  • 3+ years of hands-on Microsoft 365 engineering and administration experience.

  • Demonstrated experience performing actual Microsoft 365 migrations in production environments.

  • Experience migrating users from at least one of the following:

    • On-premises Exchange

    • Google Workspace

    • Microsoft 365 tenant

    • Third-party email platform

  • Experience with Microsoft Exchange Online.

  • Experience with Microsoft Entra ID / Azure AD.

  • Experience with Active Directory.

  • Experience with Microsoft Teams.

  • Experience with SharePoint Online.

  • Experience with OneDrive for Business.

  • Strong understanding of DNS and email routing.

  • Experience with Microsoft 365 security configuration.

  • Experience troubleshooting production Microsoft 365 environments.

Strongly Preferred Experience

  • Microsoft 365 tenant-to-tenant migrations.

  • Exchange hybrid migrations.

  • Large-scale mailbox migrations.

  • Google Workspace-to-Microsoft 365 migrations.

  • MigrationWiz or comparable third-party migration platforms.

  • Microsoft Entra Connect / Azure AD Connect.

  • Pass-through Authentication and SSO.

  • Conditional Access.

  • Microsoft Defender for Office 365.

  • Exchange Online Protection.

  • SharePoint migration tooling.

  • OneDrive migration tooling.

  • Microsoft 365 backup solutions.

  • PowerShell automation for Microsoft 365.

  • Microsoft Graph.

  • Microsoft Intune.

  • Group Policy.

  • SMTP relay architecture.

  • Exchange 2019.

  • Legacy Exchange environments.

  • Microsoft 365 security and compliance.

Technical Skill Set

The ideal candidate should have strong working knowledge of:

Microsoft Cloud

  • Microsoft 365

  • Microsoft Entra ID

  • Exchange Online

  • SharePoint Online

  • OneDrive for Business

  • Microsoft Teams

  • Microsoft Intune

  • Microsoft Defender for Office 365

  • Microsoft Purview / Data Loss Prevention

  • Microsoft 365 Groups

Identity

  • Active Directory

  • Entra Connect / Azure AD Connect

  • Directory Synchronization

  • SSO

  • Pass-through Authentication

  • MFA

  • Conditional Access

  • Self-Service Password Reset

Messaging

  • Exchange Server

  • Exchange Online

  • Exchange Hybrid

  • SMTP

  • DNS

  • Autodiscover

  • SPF

  • DKIM

  • DMARC

  • Mail-flow rules

  • Email security

Migration

  • MigrationWiz or comparable migration platforms

  • Exchange migration methodologies

  • Tenant-to-tenant migration

  • Google Workspace migration

  • SharePoint migration

  • OneDrive migration

  • Teams migration

  • Data/file migration

Automation

  • PowerShell

  • Microsoft Graph

  • Microsoft 365 administrative scripting

Education & Certifications

A bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, or a related technical discipline is preferred.

Equivalent professional experience may be accepted in place of a degree.

Preferred certifications include:

  • Microsoft Certified: Administrator Associate

  • Microsoft Certified: Identity and Access Administrator Associate

  • Microsoft Certified: Messaging Administrator Associate

  • Microsoft Certified: Teams Administrator Associate

  • Microsoft Certified: Security-related Microsoft certifications

  • Other current Microsoft 365/Azure certifications

Certifications are valuable, but demonstrated hands-on migration experience should carry greater weight than certifications alone.

Ideal Candidate Profile

The ideal candidate is a senior-level Microsoft cloud engineer who has personally executed Microsoft 365 migrations, not simply administered an established Microsoft 365 environment.

This individual should be able to walk into an unfamiliar environment, conduct discovery, identify technical dependencies, develop a migration strategy, build or validate the destination tenant, execute pilot migrations, resolve migration issues, coordinate the production cutover, validate the resulting environment, and hand the environment over to the client's IT team.

The candidate should be comfortable acting as both a technical engineer and customer-facing consultant.

They must be able to communicate complicated Microsoft technologies to technical and non-technical stakeholders, explain risks and dependencies, make sound architectural recommendations, and remain calm and methodical during production cutovers.

Critical "Must-Have" Qualifications

A candidate should not be considered fully qualified without substantial hands-on experience in the following areas:

  1. Production Microsoft 365 migrations

  2. Exchange Online

  3. Microsoft Entra ID / Azure AD

  4. Active Directory

  5. DNS and email routing

  6. Microsoft 365 identity synchronization

  7. MFA and Conditional Access

  8. Exchange migration or hybrid Exchange

  9. Microsoft Teams

  10. SharePoint Online

  11. OneDrive for Business

  12. Migration planning and cutover execution

  13. Microsoft 365 security

  14. Migration troubleshooting

  15. Technical documentation and knowledge transfer

A candidate who has only performed Microsoft 365 user administration, desktop support, Office installations, or basic account provisioning would not be considered sufficient for this role.

Work Style & Professional Attributes

  • Strong analytical and troubleshooting ability.

  • Highly organized and detail-oriented.

  • Comfortable working independently.

  • Strong written and verbal communication.

  • Customer-facing professionalism.

  • Able to work with IT managers, infrastructure engineers, security teams, and business stakeholders.

  • Able to develop and follow detailed migration plans and runbooks.

  • Comfortable working during scheduled migration and cutover windows.

  • Strong understanding of change management and production-environment risk.

  • Able to document technical work thoroughly.

  • Willing and able to take ownership of technical issues through resolution.

Project Success Criteria

The successful engineer will be expected to deliver a Microsoft 365 environment that is:

  • Properly architected.

  • Securely configured.

  • Correctly licensed.

  • Properly integrated with identity services.

  • Functionally validated.

  • Successfully migrated.

  • Properly documented.

  • Tested following migration.

  • Supported through cutover and post-migration stabilization.

  • Fully transitioned to the client's IT team through knowledge transfer and administrative training.

The engineer must ultimately leave the customer with a stable, secure, documented, and supportable Microsoft 365 environment, rather than simply completing the data migration.
